World.title: Iraq achieves wheat and date self-sufficiency for 2026: Agriculture Ministry
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture announced on Friday, September 4, 2026, that Iraq has achieved full self-sufficiency in its strategic wheat harvest for the third consecutive season, while also securing complete domestic self-sufficiency in date production.

Ministry Spokesperson Qusay Al-Hattab stated that targeted state interventions—combining climate-resilient crop genetics, subsidized modern sprinkler systems, and a data-backed agricultural calendar—have decoupled key food staples from volatile international import markets.

Core Pillars of Agricultural Self-Sufficiency

Three Consecutive Seasons of Wheat Sufficiency: The 2026 winter harvest solidified a three-year streak of domestic grain self-reliance, with the ministry already preparing its winter crop plan to maintain full coverage into 2027.

Climate-Adaptive Seed Cultivars: Agricultural research divisions successfully introduced proprietary wheat seed strains engineered to withstand high soil salinity, prolonged drought, and extreme climatic volatility.

Subsidized Irrigation Upgrades (Austrian Loan Facility): To combat persistent water scarcity across the Tigris and Euphrates basins, modern pivot and localized sprinkler systems are distributed under a 33% state subsidy. Pivot systems valued at 70 million IQD are provided to registered farmers for 49 million IQD, financed through a 10-year installment plan with a one-year grace period.

Date Palm Sector Expansion: Iraq’s date palm population expanded from roughly 12 million trees in 2003 to 22 million trees in 2026, driven by replanting campaigns and commercial orchard developments, with Zahdi dates comprising the largest share of national yield.

Agricultural Policy Framework: Modernization and Trade Protections

Policy Instrument Operational Detail Strategic Objective Wheat Support Program Salinity-tolerant seeds + subsidized machinery Eliminate grain import dependence for the national food basket. Austrian Irrigation Loan 33% unit subsidy (49M IQD net; 10-yr financing) Transition from flood irrigation to water-efficient pivot sprinklers. Date Palm Restoration Expansion to 22 million trees Reclaim historical export capacity and achieve domestic surplus. Permanent Import Bans 33 agricultural items permanently banned Protect local vegetable and fruit producers from dumping. World.title: Iraqi judiciary completes interrogation of 5,700 ISIS suspects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Supreme Judicial Council of Iraq has officially concluded the interrogation process for 5,704 ISIS detainees who were moved from northeastern Syria earlier this year, preparing them for trial.

The First Karkh Investigation Court said in a statement on Tuesday that it concluded the investigation phase of one of Iraq’s largest terrorism-related cases in history.

The verified detainees originate from 67 different nationalities, including 3,497 Syrians and 474 Iraqis.

The courts identified very dangerous agents in key leadership, military, financial, media, and security roles inside ISIS.

Six offenders were actively linked to the captivity, detention, transfer, sale, and exploitation of Yazidi women, exposing serious international crimes.

Several suspects have previously been cleared and released due to insufficient evidence linking them to terrorism crimes.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Baghdad, remain stable in Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and remained stable in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,547.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,546.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad rose, ranging between 1,552.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate remained stable, fluctuating between 1,546 and 1,545.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation represented more than a 10 percent difference in exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq exports fuel oil through Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that Iraq began exporting fuel oil shipments via Jordan for the first time last month.

Al-Rikabi explained that Iraq is exporting fuel oil through the neighboring country, not to Jordan.

The Iraqi official did not disclose the details of the agreement, its duration, or when it came into effect.

Iraqi oil shipments started flowing to Jordan in early August through the Trebil border crossing, the only land border crossing between the two countries, at a rate of 10,000 barrels per day, which were stored in the facilities of the Jordan Oil Terminals Company (JOTC), Jordan’s state-owned petroleum logistics and independent storage provider.

Through Jordan, a shipment totaling 307,000 barrels was exported to Greece.

Following the Strait of Hormuz crisis, which began with the United States’ war against Iran on February 28, Iraqi fuel oil shipments began transiting through Syria via tanker trucks, with storage at the Baniyas refinery before shipping to worldwide markets.

Between March and the end of August, Iraq exported 21.4 million barrels of fuel oil through Syria and only 307,000 barrels through Jordan.

Iraqi fuel oil exports started to increase following the Middle East conflict until the end of August in an attempt to compensate for the declining supplies via the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: 38 officers, 3,000 personnel dismissed over corruption in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Interior announced on Thursday that it permanently dismissed 38 officers and 180 personnel over administrative and financial corruption, with another 3,245 personnel discharged for desertion.

The purge represents a significant internal effort as part of the ongoing “Operation Dawn,” a nationwide anti-corruption campaign spearheaded by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The campaign has targeted numerous public officials and high-profile individuals.

According to an official statement from Miqdad Miri, the spokesperson for the Interior Ministry, the total number of individuals affected encompasses various categories of misconduct.

After receiving clear evidence of their direct involvement in bribery and financial misconduct, 38 officers were permanently removed from service.

Finalized judicial verdicts convicting 180 enlisted personnel of corruption accusations resulted in their official removal from service.

As part of larger ministry attempts to reestablish strong institutional discipline, 3,245 service personnel were discharged only for abandoning their duties.

These dismissals took place within the first 100 days of the current government’s tenure.

This security-sector cleanup is part of the larger nationwide drive “Operation Dawn.” Between late June and August, security operations resulted in the arrest of at least 210 lawmakers, public servants, and business executives.

World.title: Kenney, Sikh leader share dais as Mohan Bhagwat makes global Hindu call
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A day after telling a New York audience that a Hindu who wanted Muslims excluded from India could not remain a Hindu,

chief

Monday used his first visit to Canada to cast Hindus as builders of an âexemplary societyâ worldwide and India as a âvishwaguruâ serving humanity, not a âmahashaktiâ seeking dominance.

The speeches shared themes of oneness, but differed in emphasis. In New York, amid protests and criticism of RSS, Bhagwat addressed concerns about exclusion; in Toronto, he explained how Hindu society should organise and lead internationally without imposing its beliefs.

âThe word Hindu cannot be defined by any specific language, through any specific worship or through any living style,â he said. The dais reflected that wider outreach: former Alberta premier and federal cabinet minister Jason Kenney and Kashmir Singh Dhaliwal of the Khalsa Diwan Society joined Bhagwat, placing a senior Canadian political figure and a representative of a Sikh institution alongside the RSS chief at a gathering opposed by sections of the South Asian community.

âWe have to build our society in every country, all over the world, which is an exemplary society for the world,â Bhagwat said at the âHindu Vishwa Bandhu â Embrace the World in Friendshipâ event. The programme in Vaughan, in the Greater Toronto Area, was organised by Canadian Hindus for Outreach, Relations and Dialogue.

Presenting Indiaâs global role as one based on service rather than power, Bhagwat said: âIt became âvishwaguruâ, not âmahashaktiâ.â





Whenever help had been sought during an international crisis, he said, India had not refused. âThis is the tradition. This is the DNA of Bharat.â

Bhagwat said the RSS organised Hindus âexactly for this purpose â and nothing elseâ, describing the purpose as developing individuals who would dedicate themselves to serving humanity.

The RSS chief coupled the call for organisation with a message on civic responsibility.

People connected with India but settled elsewhere, he said, âhave to be honest, contributing citizens of that countryâ. At the same time, they should take to the world an outlook in which individuals, society and the environment could progress without harming one another.

World.title: DTC fought conductor for 32 years over Rs 67 fare and his wages, now fined Rs 1 lakh by Delhi HC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

has imposed costs of Rs 1 lakh on the Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) for pursuing a 32-year-old dispute with a bus conductor over payment of 17 months' back wages, terming the prolonged litigation an abuse of the process of law.

According to PTI report, Justice Amit Mahajan dismissed the DTC's challenge to a 2004 Industrial Tribunal order in favour of the conductor, observing that the department's continued litigation over the limited claim had resulted in avoidable expenditure of public money.

The court, in its September 2 order, said the DTC could recover the costs from the officer responsible for pursuing what it described as an "insignificant dispute".

Of the Rs 1 lakh imposed, Rs 25,000 will be paid to the Delhi High Legal Services Committee, Rs 50,000 to the PM Relief Fund and Rs 25,000 to the conductor.

What's the dispute

The dispute dates back to November 1994, when the conductor was accused of failing to issue tickets to three passengers despite collecting a total fare of Rs 67. He was suspended following the incident.

Although the enquiry officer had ruled in the conductor's favour, the disciplinary authority disagreed and issued a show-cause notice proposing his removal from service.





He was subsequently removed with effect from August 1996.

The conductor challenged the action, following which the DTC chairman-cum-managing director set aside his removal. In 1998, the DTC chairman ordered his reinstatement but denied him back wages and reduced his pay scale.

The dispute then reached the Industrial Tribunal, which in 2004 held that the punishment was illegal and without basis. It ruled that the conductor was entitled to wages on his regular pay scale, along with arrears arising from the reduced wages and regular wages for the relevant period.

The high court stayed the tribunal's order in July 2005, but Justice Mahajan found no legal ground to interfere with the tribunal's findings. The court noted that the DTC had failed to produce the enquiry report or establish a lawful basis for disagreeing with the enquiry officer.

Justice Mahajan said the tribunal had taken a "reasonable and plausible view" based on the material before it and that its findings were neither perverse nor legally unsustainable.

The court also criticised the DTC for litigating the issue of 17 months' back wages for 32 years, saying the prolonged proceedings over such a limited claim amounted to an abuse of the process of law and caused unnecessary expenditure of public money.

Every year, a child who stays in school through Class 12 rather than dropping out at 14 usually has one adult to thank for it more than any policy document: a teacher who noticed, who followed up, who made the difference between a student staying enrolled and quietly disappearing from the rolls. The Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+) 2025-26 report, released this month by the Union Ministry of Education, is built around that basic unit of the school system. It tracks how many teachers India has, how they're distributed, and what that distribution means for millions of students. The numbers show a workforce that has grown steadily even as the system around it has become leaner and retained more students.India's teacher count rose from 94,83,294 in 2022-23 to 98,07,600 in 2023-24, then to 1,01,22,420 in 2024-25 and 1,02,73,020 in 2025-26, an increase of 8.3% over four years, crossing the one-crore mark along the way. That growth is most evident in the Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR), which measures how many students each teacher is responsible for. At the Foundational level, the PTR now stands at 10 students per teacher, down from 11 in 2022-23.Preparatory has moved to 12 from 14, Middle school to 17 from 18, and Secondary to 21 from 23. All four levels are now well within the 30:1 ratio recommended under the National Education Policy; a lower PTR generally means more attention per student and classrooms that are easier to manage. The improvement has been gradual rather than sudden: Preparatory PTR, for instance, moved from 14 to 13 to 13 before settling at 12, showing the kind of steady year-on-year correction that comes from sustained recruitment rather than a one-time push.Dropout and retention figures follow the same broad trend, though not evenly across every level. Preparatory dropout fell from 8.7% in 2022-23 to 3.7%, then 2.3%, and now 1.8% in 2025-26, a decline of nearly 7 percentage points in four years. Secondary dropout came down from 13.8% to 7.0% over the same period, nearly halving. Middle school is the exception: after falling steadily from 8.1% to 5.2% to 3.5% across three years, its dropout rate ticked up slightly this year, from 3.5% to 3.6%, the only level where the four-year trend reversed rather than held.Retention tells a similar mixed story. Secondary retention jumped from 47.2% to 51.9%, helped by more schools now offering secondary education, and Middle retention rose from 82.8% to 83.7%, continuing a climb from 75.8% in 2022-23. Foundational retention eased this year, from 98.9% to 98.5%, after three straight years of gains from 92.1% in 2022-23. Preparatory retention also slipped, from 92.4% to 91.1% â but unlike Foundational, its four-year path wasn't a steady climb: it fell to 85.4% in 2023-24 before recovering to 92.4% the year after, and now sits only marginally above where it started in 2022-23, at 90.9%.Enrolment and transition numbers add to the picture. Secondary GER rose from 68.5% to 71.7% this year; across the four-year period it actually dipped to 66.5% in 2023-24 before climbing back and past its 2022-23 level of 67.6%. Middle GER has stayed roughly flat for four years, moving between 89.5% and 90.3% and settling at 89.6% now. Transition rates â the share of students who move on to the next stage rather than leaving school altogether â improved at every checkpoint: Foundational-to-Preparatory transition rose to 99.2% from 98.6%, Preparatory-to-Middle to 93.8% from 92.2%, and Middle-to-Secondary to 88.3% from 86.6%, each figure now at its highest point across the four years tracked.The growth in teacher numbers has also changed how schools are staffed. Single-teacher schools, where one person handles every grade and subject, fell by about 3% in 2025-26 to 1,00,843, continuing a decline from 1,18,190 in 2022-23 and 1,10,971 the year after. Zero-enrolment schools fell even faster â by around 29% in a single year, from 7,993 to 5,663, though the number had actually risen to 12,954 in 2023-24 before the sharp correction that followed. The report attributes both declines to how UDISE+ data itself is used, allowing planners to reallocate teachers to where enrolment actually needs them, rather than leaving schools overstaffed relative to the students they serve.School infrastructure has improved along with the workforce. Computer access rose from 47.7% in 2022-23 to 69.9% in 2025-26, with the sharpest single-year jump, a 9.5 percentage point rise, coming in 2023-24. Internet access followed a close path, up from 49.7% to 67.4% over the same period. Basic facilities are now close to universal: 95.0% of schools have electricity, up from 91.7%; 99.5% have drinking water; 98.5% have girls' toilets and 97.2% have boys' toilets; and 96.9% have handwashing facilities, up from 94.1% four years ago. Library access has also grown steadily, from 88.3% to 90.5% of schools. Two areas lag behind the rest â playgrounds, present in 81.9% of schools, actually declined slightly from 83.0% the previous year, breaking an otherwise uninterrupted rise since 2022-23, and rainwater harvesting remains available in just 29.9% of schools despite steady incremental gains each year since a base of 28.0% in 2022-23. Ramps and handrails for students with disabilities have grown from 51.0% to 58.2% of schools, though more than four in ten schools still lack them.The report also points to a shift in who is doing the teaching. Women now make up 54.9% of India's teachers, up from 52.3% four years ago and 53.3% the year after that â a steady climb of more than two-and-a-half percentage points across a workforce of over a crore people.Girls' enrolment has moved more slowly but just as consistently, from 48.0% in 2022-23 to 48.1%, then 48.3%, and now 48.4% in 2025-26 â small annual shifts that add up to real change in a system enrolling tens of millions of students each year.Read together, the UDISE+ 2025-26 numbers show a system that added capacity, tightened ratios and expanded infrastructure over four years, while still carrying a few gaps that didn't move like the rest of the data â a middle-school dropout rate that rose instead of fell, a Foundational and Preparatory retention dip after years of improvement, a zero-enrolment number that spiked before it fell, and a playground shortfall the other infrastructure numbers don't quite explain. None of these gaps undoes the larger trend, but they're the parts of the report worth watching in the years ahead, since they mark the points where the steady four-year climb didn't hold.

World.title: Work-life balance vs job security: The workplace trade-off Gen Z is challenging
World.content:
Young workers are entering a labour market shaped by layoffs, artificial intelligence, intense competition and constantly changing skill requirements. At the same time, they have grown increasingly vocal about boundaries, mental health and the value of time outside the office.

As the generational composition of the workforce continues to evolve, organisations seem to face new challenges in designing effective employee engagement strategies. Shaped by rapid technological change and globalisation, millennials and Generation Z bring distinct work values, communication preferences and expectations around career growth, flexibility and the workplace.

For Gen Z, the ideal job increasingly sounds like a carefully negotiated deal: pay me well, give me room to grow, let me have a life after work and, preferably, give me some control over how I get the work done.

A survey of young workers reflects that tension. Job security emerged as an important consideration, but work-life balance carried an equally strong pull. The responses suggest a generation trying to answer a difficult question: how much career stability is worth sacrificing personal freedom for?

The survey found that 95% of respondents rated job security at the higher end of the importance scale, with 57.1% giving it the highest rating.





At the same time, 90.5% also gave work-life balance equal weight.

That makes the dilemma rather clear. Gen Z wants security. It also wants breathing room.

The salary still matters

The idea of Gen Z choosing lifestyle over money tells only one part of the story. The responses from young workers point to a more complicated calculation.

Financial independence and building a successful career were each selected by 76.2% of respondents as among their biggest reasons for working.

Achieving a particular lifestyle followed at 61.9%, while gaining experience and skills came in at 57.1%.

Money remains a major part of the equation. Neeshu Shukla, a working professional from Delhi, said, âBetter pay is important. Money is the deal breaker,â followed by timely hikes and promotions.

For Shukla, however, the workplace equation extends beyond the payslip. She wants a professional but empathetic environment and opportunities to learn and grow.

She also places value on skills, experience, capabilities and willingness to learn as the basis for determining an employeeâs value.

The broader survey reflects a similar hierarchy. Personal growth was the most-selected career priority apart from money, at 85.7%. Work-life balance followed at 66.7%, while good workplace culture stood at 61.9%. Career progression and job security were selected by 47.6% and 42.9%, respectively.

Security feels increasingly fragile

The anxiety around stability also has a very practical source. Competition and low salaries were the biggest source of career insecurity in the survey, selected by 76.2% of respondents. Layoffs followed at 52.4%, while lack of job opportunities and lack of career growth each stood at 47.6%. Economic uncertainty was another concern for 42.9% of respondents. AI and automation were cited by 38.1%.

That anxiety shows up in how respondents view the very idea of a âsecure jobâ.

More than seven in 10 said such security exists only in certain industries. Just 19% considered a secure job realistic in the broader economy.

A recent Emeritus report titled âIndiaâs Gen Z Outlook 2026â found a similar shift in how young Indians think about careers. The study found that 74% of Gen Z respondents prioritise work-life balance over formal leadership titles, while 65% believe a successful career does not require becoming an executive leader.

That finding adds another layer to the workplace debate. The traditional image of career success often comes with a predictable sequence: climb the ladder, take on more responsibility, earn more money and eventually reach a senior title.

Gen Z appears to be questioning how attractive that ladder remains.

Ashwin Damera, co-founder and CEO of Emeritus, described the shift as an overhaul of the traditional career path, driven by rapidly changing skills and jobs.

How much sacrifice is acceptable?

The survey becomes particularly interesting when the questions move from preferences to trade-offs.

Asked whether they would stay in a job they disliked if it offered excellent job security and financial stability, 19% said probably yes. Another 33.3% remained unsure, while 42.9% said probably not.

Over 42% of respondents said they would immediately leave a high-paying job that seriously affected their mental health or personal life.

A further 19% said their decision would depend on their financial situation.

For Kajal Singh, an HR professional working at a consultancy firm in Delhi, the workplace she wants comes down to âflexible work options, better work-life balance & a supportive environment.â

Harshita, a working professional from Bhopal, takes the idea of flexibility further. In her ideal workplace, she wants âflexibility and respect for the opinions of Gen Zs,â along with room for employees to decide how they execute their work.

The pattern is not confined to India. A separate Deloitte 2026 survey of Gen Zs and millennials found that 55% of Gen Zs and 52% of millennials are delaying major life decisions because of financial pressures. Only 25% of Gen Zs and 21% of millennials prefer rapid career progression through frequent promotions, while just 6% in both groups identify leadership as their primary career goal.

At the same time, 74% of both Gen Zs and millennials use AI to some extent in their day-to-day work, with many viewing it as an opportunity to improve productivity and open new career paths â even as they feel they are adapting faster than their organisations.

Taken together, the findings point to a generation caught between two competing demands: the need for financial security and the refusal to define success solely by the traditional career ladder.

The stereotype problem

The generation also appears to be tired of having that negotiation interpreted as a lack of ambition.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

More than half of respondents said older generations completely misunderstand Gen Zâs attitude towards work, while another 42.9% said they misunderstand it somewhat.

The most irritating stereotype was the idea that âGen Z doesn't want to workâ, selected by 81% of respondents. âGen Z quits too easilyâ followed at 76.2%. Other commonly selected stereotypes included being lazy, expecting too much and having no loyalty.

What does the survey indicate?

For employers, that makes the Gen Z workplace conversation less about choosing between stability and balance and more about whether the two can exist together. For young workers, the bigger challenge is figuring out which compromises build a career and which ones slowly consume the life that career was supposed to support.

World.title: Output overdrive: 30% productivity boost could power 35% of future manufacturing
World.content:
India's manufacturing sector could get nearly 35 per cent of its future output simply by getting its workforce 30 per cent more productive.

The finding comes from KPMG's analysis of more than 130 large Indian manufacturing companies over 10 years.

It found that companies which improved productivity faster than their peers also saw stronger growth in profits and market value.

Their net profits grew by around 10-11 per cent annually, compared with about 7 per cent for companies with average productivity.

The difference was even wider in market value. Companies leading in productivity recorded around 19 per cent CAGR in market capitalisation, against nearly 10 per cent for average-productivity organisations.

Overall, productivity-leading companies saw more than 50 per cent higher profitability growth and twice the market-cap expansion compared with their peers.

Small factories lag larger firms

The gains, however, are not spread evenly across the manufacturing sector.

More than 70 per cent of large manufacturing companies would need transformative measures to achieve the productivity growth rate required for India's manufacturing ambition, the report said.





There is also a wide gap between smaller and larger factories. Small and unorganised manufacturing facilities produce less than 20 per cent of the output per worker compared with large firms.

Even among companies within the manufacturing sector, productivity can vary sharply, with differences ranging between 300 per cent and 1,000 per cent.

Six ways to drive manufacturing growth

KPMG identified six broad levers for manufacturing growth:

Productivity

Workforce shifts

Global integration

Investment in capacity

Innovation and technology

Consumption-led growth.

But productivity stands out because its benefits can continue over time.

âProductivity is Indian manufacturing's most powerful growth lever,â the report said, adding that productivity gains âembed permanently into the system, raising output, margins, and competitiveness year after year.â

âUnlike scale or demand-led levers, productivity improvements embed permanently into the system,â the report said.

The report said improving productivity would require companies to rethink how work is organised, how organisations are structured and how their workforce is deployed.

Digital and AI tools, performance management and changes in workplace culture would also be needed to support these changes, it said.

World.title: Census 2027: The 14 questions and why opposition fears an NPR 'backdoor'
World.content:
Opposition is also raising questions over the methodology of population enumeration, alleging that it too has a âdeeper nefarious purposeâ

What is the controversy?

What are the opposition's charges

Difference between Census and NPR

Can Census data be shared?

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Although six years late, enumerators have started knocking on doors for the decennial headcount in Ladakh and snowbound regions such as Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand starting September 1.But doubts and fears have preceded the Census, turning what was meant to be a routine exercise to track population growth and aid policy planning into a fresh political flashpoint.Until now, the caste census had been the main point of contention between the opposition and the government. The opposition had questioned the intent and methodology of an exercise being conducted in the country after almost 100 years.The contention has now moved beyond the caste census, and the opposition is also raising questions over the methodology of population enumeration, alleging that it too has a âdeeper nefarious purposeâ.On August 14, the Centre notified the list of questions that officials will ask during population enumeration. The questionnaire, however, contains 14 new or modified questions compared with the 2011 Census.These include spouse's name, nationality as declared, father's particulars, mother's particulars, SC/ST/caste, literacy and digital literacy, highest educational level attained and stream/discipline, place of Covid-19 vaccination, total number of bank accounts, mobile number, Aadhaar number, voter ID number, passport number for Indian passport holders, and availability of a driving licence.Interestingly, several of these questions, including details of a person's father and mother and their places of birth, were also part of the National Population Register (NPR) schedule notified in 2020.Moreover, the Union Budget presented on February 1 this year allocated Rs 6,000 crore for the NPR and Census 2027, even though the government has not yet notified any schedule for the NPR.The Budget document said the allocation included provisions for the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India and various schemes of the Registrar General of India, with Rs 6,000 crore earmarked for NPR and Census 2027.Following the notification of the questionnaire, the opposition has accused the Centre of turning the Census exercise into a âbackdoor for the NPR, and eventually, NRCâ.Congress Rajya Sabha member Jairam Ramesh said the methodology of asking questions in Census 2027 is flawed and alleged that questions on religion, date of birth, place of birth and parents' details had never been asked in previous enumerations.âCensus is confidential. Clearly, Census 27 has a deeper nefarious purpose,â he said in a post on X.Similarly, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee alleged that the Centre was planning to conduct the Census in the form of NPR.âThey have started the census. Census in the form of NPR. You have to provide your bank account number, mobile number and Aadhaar number. You must disclose the full details of all family members,â Mamata said.âNo political party has been informed. At least the Trinamool Congress was not informed. Nobody knows whose name will be deleted. Is it going to be another SIR? Who knows,â she added.Even during the run-up to the Bengal assembly elections, she alleged that the Centre was planning to 'take away' people's citizenship in the name of NRC.Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan also raised questions over the inclusion of the new questions, arguing that the Census should not be used to divide people.âThe reported inclusion of questions about parentsâ place of birth and religion in the upcoming Census is deeply troubling. The Census must not become a backdoor for the NPR and, eventually, the NRC. Citizenship cannot be tied to religion, and no census should be used to divide our people. The Union Government must immediately drop such divisive questions. Secular forces must stand united against this dangerous move,â Vijayan said.Census and NPR differ in their legal basis, objectives and the nature of information they are designed to collect.The Census is a statistical exercise meant to produce data on population, literacy, occupation, migration, housing and, in 2027, caste. It is used for making policies, allocating resources and delimitation.On the other hand, the National Population Register is a continuously updated register of âusual residentsâ created under the Citizenship Act, 1955.It is designed to maintain an identifiable database of people who have lived in a locality for at least six months or intend to stay there for the next six months, irrespective of their citizenship.The NPR collects detailed identity information, including names, parents' particulars, place of birth, nationality as declared, address and identity documents such as Aadhaar, voter ID and passport, as well as mobile numbers. The data collected through NPR is linked to the proposed National Register of Citizens.Under Rule 3 of the Citizenship Rules, the Centre may order preparation of the National Population Register, from which the Local Register of citizens is prepared after verification.Rule 4 provides that individuals whose citizenship is doubtful can be flagged in the Population Register for further enquiry.The NPR data was first collected in 2010 alongside the 2011 Census house-listing exercise and updated through a door-to-door survey in 2015.However, both the Census and NPR are conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Union Ministry of Home Affairs.The inclusion of the new questions has raised a larger question: Can information collected during the Census be accessed or used by government agencies for purposes beyond the exercise itself?The law says no. Section 15 of the Census Act, 1948 provides a strong legal shield around personal information collected during the Census.âNo person shall have a right to inspect any book, register or record made by a census-officer in the discharge of his duty,â the Act says.âNo entry in any such book, register, record or schedule shall be admissible as evidence in any civil proceeding whatsoever or in any criminal proceeding other than a prosecution under this Act or any other law for any act or omission which constitutes an offence under this Act,â it further says.This means that the information collected through the census cannot be used by other government agencies to determine the citizenship of a person.Speaking to The Times of India, advocate Ajinkya Udane said it would therefore be incorrect to accuse the government of divulging information collected through the Census.âThrough the census, private information of people is being asked. However, the Census Act bars the government from divulging this information to its agencies,â Udane said.âSo, to accuse the government of doing something which the law bars it from doing is not correct,â he added.Cyber and privacy law expert advocate Prashant Mali, however, stressed that Census data must remain a statistical instrument and ânot become a backdoor for state surveillanceâ.âSection 15 of the Census Act creates a strong statutory confidentiality barrier. Individual census records are not open to inspection and are not admissible as evidence. Therefore, census information cannot legitimately be converted into an evidentiary database for citizenship determination merely because another government authority wants to use it,â Mali said.He said that even if a census record, or personal information traceable back to it, is accessed or used in a manner prohibited by Section 15, describing it as âindependent intelligenceâ would not cure the underlying violation.âSubstance must prevail over form. If the underlying census record or identifiable information has been accessed or used contrary to Section 15, I feel calling it independent intelligence does not cure the problem,â he said.âI feel the State cannot do indirectly through a citizenship inquiry what Section 15 of the Census Act prohibits it from doing directly through the Census record. A lawful purpose for processing does not automatically create a lawful source of data,â he told The Times of India.During the conversation, Mali said that the interaction between the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) and the Census Act will also be interesting to watch during the exercise.âDPDPA (Digital Personal Data Protection Act) Sections 3â17 are scheduled to come into force 18 months after 13 November 2025, i.e. 13 May 2027, while Census 2027 field operations occur around that period,â Mali said.âThis makes the interaction between the Census Act and DPDPA particularly interesting for the 2027 exercise,â he added.The Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) is primary law which will dictate how the personal data is collected, processed and stored.It sets out obligations for entities handling personal data - such as obtaining consent, limiting use to the stated purpose, and ensuring data security - and grants individuals rights over their own data, including access and correction.

World.title: No registration number, no attendance: NMC warns medical colleges
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Medical colleges have one month to update the National Medical Register (NMR) or State Medical Register (SMR) numbers of their faculty and specified teaching staff on the Aadhaar Enabled Biometric Attendance System (AEBAS), failing which their daily attendance could be blocked and automatically rejected.

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has warned that this may adversely impact the compliance status of the medical college during NMC assessments and inspections.

The warning was issued on September 3 after the NMC found that nodal officers at several medical colleges had left the NMR or SMR registration-number field blank while registering faculty on the attendance portal.

The commission has directed colleges to review and update the profiles of all medical faculty, Junior Residents, Senior Residents, tutors and demonstrators with correct and valid NMR or SMR numbers.

For non-medical faculty and tutors or demonstrators holding Master of Science (MSc) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) qualifications, colleges have been instructed to enter âNAâ in the registration-number field.

The NMC has made it clear that leaving the registration-number field blank will not be permitted.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The directive effectively makes faculty registration details part of the attendance compliance process, rather than a routine profile correction.





The memorandum has been sent to deans, principals and directors of all medical colleges and institutions, besides state and Union Territory medical education departments, directorates of medical education and State Medical Councils.

The move is under the provisions of the Undergraduate and Postgraduate Minimum Standard Requirements and Medical Assessment and Rating Board regulations, which provide for periodic, transparent and digitally verified assessment of teaching staff in medical institutions.

World.title: 'Some calling for tariff barriers to go up arbitrarily without economic logic': Belgian PM takes veiled dig at Trump
World.content:
Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever took a veiled dig at

over his decision to impose tariffs saying many voices are now calling for tariff barriers to go up but they do it arbitrarily.

De Wever said the India-European Union (EU) Free Trade Agreement (FTA) made both sides resilient against disruption and coercion.

âLadies and gentlemen, more and more voices today are calling for barriers to go up, for markets to be shut off, for tariffs to be imposed. Some do this entirely arbitrarily. They decide something on Monday, they revoke it on Wednesday and reinstall on Saturday. You all know who I am talking about.

I am not going to say the name but you know these people arbitrarily do it without any economic logic at all,â De Wever said without naming Trump. Wever was in Mumbai for the IndiaâBelgium High-Level Dialogue on the IndiaâEU Free Trade Agreement (FTA). Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the India-EU FTA was a win-win for everyone. CM Devendra Fadnavis said India EU FTA will fundamentally change the India EU relationship Maharashtra should become the demonstrative state for the India EU FTA implementation.





Wever said PM Narendra Modi is a wise leader, and one of the most inspiring world leaders. âAntwerp is pocket sized Mumbai in Belgium. We are sailing through rough waters but India and the EU have chosen partnership. We have concluded the mother of all deals. It is an expression of mutual respect. Our cooperation is directed towards international order. The FTA arrives at a critical moment. To make trading partnerships more predictable.

If every community in Belgium is like the Indian community I would be a happy Prime Minister,â De Wever said.

Goyal said the India EU FTA was in the making for 25 years. âIt is a win-win agreement, it will open opportunities for farmers, start ups, women entrepreneurs, it has something for everyone. Itâs been deftly negotiated protecting sensitive sectors on both sides. It offers huge potential for both sides," Goyal said.

â66% Indiaâs data center capacity is in Maharashtra. We want Belgium to be part of Maharashtraâs journey to a trillion dollar economy. We have bilateral trade of 13.8 billion USD. But it understates the potential. Maharashtra would like to contribute and be the principal engine of this growth story. I want to make a direct invitation. If Belgium companies are looking at India for investment after the FTA, look and come to Maharashtra.

We have a manufacturing ecosystem. This should become a template for Belgium - Maharashtra partnerships,â Fadnavis said.

Fadnavis said Maharashtra would like to be the first state to translate the FTA into action. âBelgium Maharashtra projects must be fast tracked. If Belgium companies identifies - project, we will dedicate a team and work with Belgium to make it happen. Come to Maharashtra and from Maharashtra serve India and the world.

Maharashtra is volunteering to convert strategic direction into action,â Fadnavis said.

World.title: Russian President Vladimir Putin orders 72-hour pause in strikes on Kyiv
World.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has ordered a 72-hour pause in strikes on Kyiv, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russia's Tass news agency Saturday (September 5, 2026).

“Putin has ordered that no strikes be carried out against Kyiv for three days, starting at midnight today,” Mr. Peskov said.

He said the decision was tied to preparations for U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to visit Kyiv for peace talks.

World.title: Climate scientist Krishna AchutaRao dies at 62
World.content:
Krishna AchutaRao, a leading voice in climate and atmospheric sciences and professor at the Centre for Atmospheric Sciences, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi, died on September 4, 2026. He was 62.

Among his key contributions were determining the degree to which observed climatic change could be attributed to human activity. Over the years, his collaborative work with several scientists demonstrated detectable human influence on temperature changes across Indian sub-regions. This played a key role in connecting global climate science with the regional risks confronting India.

“Krishna was a long-time friend and colleague, and over the years, we had many conversations and arguments about climate science. He was also a clear and principled critic whenever scientific temper was compromised, something that has become increasingly important in the present political climate, “ Roxy Mathew Koll, climate scientist at the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, Pune, told The Hindu, adding, “His passing is a major loss to Indian climate science, but for many of us it is also the loss of a warm, thoughtful friend with a wonderful sense of humour. I will miss him deeply.”

In his two decades at IIT Delhi, he served as Head of the Centre for Atmospheric Sciences and Dean (Faculty), helping establish the institute’s Centre of Excellence for Climate Change Adaptation. An engineering graduate, he worked at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory’s Program for Climate Model Diagnosis and Intercomparison in the U.S., before returning to India in 2007.

“Krishna was a wonderful person and, of late, worked on the attribution of climate events like heat waves. He also applied AI tools in climate change and monsoon research. We will miss him,” Madhavan Rajeevan, Vice Chancellor, ATRIA University, and former Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, told The Hindu.

He was also a member of the World Climate Research Programme’s Joint Scientific Committee from 2025.

“I completed my Ph.D. under his supervision and it is extremely difficult for me to accept this loss,” Dileepkumar R., Assistant Professor, Kumbalathu Sankupillai Memorial Devaswom Board College, Kerala, said in an email, adding, “He was much more than a Ph.D. supervisor to me…a man of great integrity, a genuinely kind soul, an exceptional scientist, and a person with a deep commitment to society.”

World.title: Salem Railway Division collects ₹2.48 crore through ticket-checking drive in August
World.content:
The Salem Railway Division (SRD) collected ₹2.48 crore through ticket-checking drives in August.

In a release on Saturday (September 5), the SRD said the ticket-checking squads of the Salem Division conducted regular checks onboard trains and on railway premises to detect various malpractices. During such checks, they detected cases of persons travelling without a ticket, irregular travel, unbooked luggage, etc. and levied penalties accordingly.

In August, the ticket-checking squads of the division detected 11,826 cases of ticketless travel and collected an amount of ₹1.32 crore in penalty, an increase of 18% in the amount collected compared with the corresponding period last year. In August 2025, the division collected an amount of ₹1.11 crore in penalty.

Moreover, 14,455 cases of irregular travel were also found in August, and an amount of ₹1.15 crore was collected in penalty from passengers, marking an increase of 17.4% in cases detected and 64.5% in the amount collected in penalty against the same period last year. In August 2025, the division detected 12,316 cases of irregular travel and collected an amount of ₹70.35 lakh in penalty.

Similarly, in August 2026, 95 cases of unbooked luggage/carrying luggage exceeding the permitted quantity were detected. The penalty levied for these cases was ₹40,223. This is an increase of 27% in cases detected compared with the same period last year. In August 2025, the division detected 75 cases of unbooked luggage.

World.title: Divine Delicacies to unravel history behind festive foods
World.content:
“Every dish on your plate has a story, a history and politics,” says Aparna Jaishankar, host of Divine Delicacies, an upcoming storytelling and menu tasting event at Atta Galatta, Bengaluru on September 6. As a performance storyteller and an educator, her series of performances have revolved around Indian mythology, heritage, history and philosophy.

This initiative, Divine Delicacies, is the result of discussions between Aparna Jaishankar and Lakshmi and Subodh Shankar, the co-founders of Atta Galatta. Taking place for over two years, Aparna’s performances under this banner have always revolved around food, but never in their singularity.

A thought that ignited this spark were the stories behind the food of the divine; food considered sacred or offered as prasadam in temples, during festivals, for deities or to the region specific “under the tree gods”.

Scheduled a week before Ganesh Chaturthi, this edition, will feature food from well-known festival feasts to lesser-known prasadams. “ The hall is decorated as ambience plays a vital role in experiencing the authenticity of our heritage,” says Aparna, adding, “The taste differs between eating off a plate, a banana leaf or a dona patta (areca or palm leaf).”

The venue can accommodate around 15 to 18 people, making the experience exclusive and intimate. The food that is served is neither commercially prepared nor store bought but will be prepared in Lakshmi and Subodh’s personal kitchen.

The heritage of these delicacies will be narrated alongside the prasadam being served during the two-hour session. The menu has been curated keeping in mind both the plausibility of preparation, and the availability of authentic ingredients.

Needless to say, research played a major role in this project. What is the story of the dish? Where can you find it? These are some of the questions that will be answered during the session. Though the dishes at every session might change depending on narrative requirements, what remains constant is the dessert. After all, as Aparna says, “How can one talk about food without the perfect dessert to top it off?”

Divine Delicacies is scheduled to take place on September 6, at 12:30pm at Atta Galatta, Indiranagar. The tickets start at ₹500. For further details visit attagalatta.com

World.title: School Education Department orders inquiry into SGT appointment under Sports Quota in Kurnool district
World.content:
The Department of School Education has initiated an inquiry into the appointment of Ediga Prabhakar as a Secondary Grade Teacher (SGT-Telugu) under the Sports Quota in Mega DSC-2025 in Kurnool district.

Director of School Education Thameem Ansariya said in a statement that the department had taken suo motu cognisance of media reports alleging irregularities in Mr. Prabhakar’s selection and subsequent posting at the MPPS (New), Vallur, in Kowthalam mandal.

Following the reports, the Kurnool District Educational Officer (DEO) initiated an inquiry and sought all relevant records and verification documents pertaining to the candidate’s selection and appointment. The records were being examined as part of a detailed scrutiny of the case, she said.

Further action would be taken by the competent authority after receiving and examining the inquiry report. Any action, if warranted, would be strictly in accordance with the applicable recruitment and service rules, Ms. Ansariya said.

She reiterated that the School Education Department was committed to maintaining transparency, merit-based selection and integrity throughout the Mega DSC-2025 recruitment process.

“The inquiry is aimed at establishing the facts and ensuring that the recruitment norms were followed,” she said.

World.title: New West Bengal tourism logo faces criticism
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Friday (September 4, 2026) unveiled a new State tourism logo and highlighted his government’s push towards better infrastructure development. Meanwhile, the new logo has faced criticism for the quality of work and design.

The new logo goes has the tagline “West Bengal – Where India feels different”, changed from the old Trinamool Congress-era tagline “Experience Bengal - The Sweetest Part of India”. The Tourism Department’s new theme, “Dekhbo Natun Rupe, Dekhbo Natun Chokhe [See in a new light, see with a new vision]” was also launched at the same event at the Dhono Dhanyo auditorium in Kolkata.

Mr. Adhikari said that his government has allotted ₹500 crore in this fiscal year for the development of tourism in the State. He added that there is a need to push for better tourism infrastructure development to attract more visitors.

“At one point West Bengal used to be a preferred travel destination. But during the last 15 years, here, we have destroyed our nature and tourism infrastructure. That is why now tourists prefer other States as travel destinations,” Mr. Adhikari said, while adding that they will increase manpower in this industry to enhance the infrastructure.

They will also focus on revamping the government’s tourist guesthouses to attract more tourists. The government will also push to make transportation better to help boost the tourism sector.

“We will procure 11 new boats that will be used for water tourism from Babughat on the Ganges to Gangasagar and other small islands. There are also plans to plant 20 lakh mangrove saplings in the Sundarbans,” the Chief Minister further said.

Mr. Adhikari said the State will collaborate with the Centre to get better ideas for the development of tourism.

New logo attracts criticism on social media

However, the new logo faced massive criticism on social media with many calling the work “immature”. Netizens across multiple social media sites came down heavily on the logo, asking why the promotional video does not feature places from West Bengal, and rather shows multiple places from foreign countries.

Former Governor of Tripura Tathagata Roy posted the video of the logo launch on his social media and said that the work was “very stupid and amateurish”.

“Why should scenes from Moscow, Egypt and Rio de Janiero feature in a video on West Bengal? And ‘how India feels different’! Is it trying to showcase West Bengal or the whole of India? This video does disservice to the achievements of the BJP government of West Bengal,” Mr. Roy wrote in his post. He also asked for the video to be taken down immediately.

Meanwhile, Trinamool MP Derek O’Brien wrote in a social media post: “TRASH is a mild word for this communication.”

World.title: Nepal flash floods: Death toll rises to 1,344
World.content:
The death toll due to the devastating flash floods in Nepal rose to 1,344 on Saturday (September 5, 2026) as more bodies were recovered from the affected areas while thousands remain missing, police said.

According to the data released by the Nepal Police, a total of 843 bodies have been successfully recovered, consisting of 758 adults and 85 children.

Also read | Nepal’s agony, the Himalayan warning to India

Additionally, authorities also reported having retrieved 501 amputated bodies from the flood-hit areas.

The death toll in the flash floods on Saturday (September 5, 2026) rose to 1,344 with the recovery of more bodies, Nepal Police said in a statement.

The flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal, leaving a trail of destruction.

So far, 1,030 bodies have been managed by temporarily burying them underground as per specified regulations such as DNA collection.

The joint rescue teams led by the Nepal Army have continued their search and rescue efforts on the eleventh day on Saturday, with the number of missing people estimated at 4,898.

World.title: Telangana CM Revanth and TCS announce ₹70,000 crore AI Data Centre in Future City
World.content:
Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on Saturday announced ₹70,000-crore investment by the Tata Group, TCS and HyperVault in Telangana that would create the largest data centre in the country, creating direct employment to 7,000 people.

The Chief Minister also set a deadline of June 2, 2028, the Telangana Formation Day, for the inauguration of what he described as India’s largest AI data centre. “From groundbreaking to inauguration, exactly 21 months from today, on June 2, 2028, we want to inaugurate India’s largest AI data centre,” he said.

Recalling his interaction with Chairman of Tata Sons N. Chandrasekaran, at the World Economic Forum in Davos in January 2026, Mr. Reddy said he had requested him to bring “big news” for Telangana in terms of investment. “He smiled and accepted. He promised me that he would announce it shortly,” Mr. Reddy said.

That is why the government had refrained from announcing the investment until the Tata Group formally made the announcement. The project would constitute one of the largest investments in artificial intelligence and Future City.

As per the announcement, the TCS data centre subsidiary HyperVault will develop a large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) data centre campus with capacity of up to 1 gigawatt (GW).

The Chief Minister also sought to assure investors that Telangana would maintain continuity in its investment policies despite changes in governments. He referred to the policy continuity under successive governments in undivided Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and said governments had improved existing policies rather than abandoning them.

“There is no policy paralysis in my State. I don’t want to create any confusion. I want to give you more and more confidence and political differences and ideological differences will not affect the investments policy,” he said.

Radial Road-1 dedicated to Ratan Tata

Mr. Reddy said the 50-km Radial Road-1, connecting the Outer Ring Road with Future City through Kongara Kalan, would be among the best roads in India and could even be used as an emergency runway.

He said the road had been dedicated to Bharat Ratna award winner Ratan Tata and recalled his announcement at the Telangana Rising Global Summit that the road would be dedicated to an organisation investing ₹1 lakh crore in the State.

CEO and Managing Director of TCS K Krithivasan, said AI was not a technology disruption but a civilisational shift. It will change everything we do today, and societies that transition would be at the forefront, while India has a great opportunity to catch up.

CTO of OpenAI Uday Rudraraju addressed the meeting virtually. K Rajanna, president of TCS HyperVault and CEO of Hypervault Deepesh Nanda were present along with IT Minister D Sridhar Babu, Ministers Uttam Kumar Reddy, Komatireddy Venkata Reddy and Adluri Lakshman Kumar. Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju and Government Advisor K. Ramakrishna Rao were also present.

World.title: Naqvi says new administrative units to be formed only with people's consent
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Saturday said that any new administrative units in the country would only be formed if the people voiced their support for such a move.

Addressing the National Policy Dialogue in Lahore, he said, “Reset does not mean breaking the system. Under no circumstances does it mean breaking the system. It means that whatever is wrong should be changed.”

Naqvi stressed that the changes should be brought through “political consensus” and “according to the will of our people”. He added that if the nation did not want the new administrative units, they would not be created.

He emphasised that such a change could not be brought about only based on the will of an individual, a political party or a government.

“And this would only happen if the people want it and consent to it,” he maintained.

The interior minister called for a dialogue that would consider the positive and negative aspects of new units. “Draft a thing and present it to the people, asking them whether they accept it or not.”

On the question of how many new administrative units should be created with what territorial limits, Naqvi emphasised the need to review their “benefits, methods and financial consequences”.

“Most importantly, our parliament, experts and those people responsible for it should debate on it, and finally, we must seek our public’s opinion.”

The minister clarified that his comments from last month were not about any particular political party, but rather about the “system” that has been in place since the country’s independence.

Naqvi called for undertaking the proposed administrative reforms as per the Constitution. “It has to be done through democratic means.”

“Under no circumstances are we ready to accept that we have become so incapable that we cannot reset this system,” he said, calling for political parties to hold deliberations on the matter.

The interior minister asserted he would not abandon the idea, adding that many “emotional” speeches were being made about the administrative units.

He urged politicians not to get emotional about the topic, adding that the change was not one that would happen overnight.

The minister contended that the country’s administrative system had lost its effectiveness and its “impact is not reaching the public at all”.

Acknowledging administrative issues, Naqvi said, “Even today, four out of every 10 children are not receiving the education they need. Today, only 55 per cent of the population has access to clean drinking water, and there are still two million cases pending in our courts.”

These were the issues that the government was trying to rectify, he contended.

Describing himself as the “biggest supporter of Islamabad province”, Naqvi called for the federal capital to receive its share of the National Finance Commission (NFC) Award.

“Islamabad is the only city that does not get a single rupee from the budget of Pakistan,” he insisted, adding that declaring Islamabad a province would give its citizens their rights.

The minister also highlighted the population factor in the disbursement of the NFC award, saying it remained an “incentive” for provinces. “That incentive is present till today, so are we waiting for that bomb to explode? […] Does this not need to be reset?”

Naqvi further said, “Governments keep changing; policies keep changing; budgets come and go; and we keep making plans. But the biggest issue is how much we are able to deliver in the end.”

He added that if, despite all the potential that Pakistan has, “we are still not getting the results, it is necessary to reset it (the system)”.

Citing New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani as an example, Naqvi said the politicians who came to power as mayors knew their citizens and their problems the best.

The minister stressed that the proposed reforms would aim to empower the people. He said a Sindhi would remain Sindhi and a Punjabi would remain Punjabi. “No one will be asked to surrender their identity,” he assured the public.

He added that the discussion on the proposed reforms was not supposed to be based on generational, tribal or regional divides. “Its aim is improved governance, a competent system and bringing people closer to the government.”

Concluding his address, Naqvi reiterated: “In no circumstances should we stray from the will of the people. All political parties will have to deliberate on this. It cannot be one person’s issue or one province’s decision.”

He added, “If this is what the public wants, then it will happen no matter what.”

In July, Naqvi had proposed a dialogue among all political parties to bring about reforms to the current governance system, while also calling for new provinces and urgent administrative reforms.

His comments had ignited an animated debate across the country, with the PPP referring the question to its top decision-making forum, the Sindh chief minister flatly rejecting it, Lahore’s lawyers terming it unconstitutional and Sindhi nationalist groups demanding the minister’s resignation.

World.title: Police charge sheet says building management at fault for Gul Plaza inferno
World.content:
KARACHI: Police on Saturday submitted a charge sheet before the South judicial magistrate on the Gul Plaza fire, blaming the building management’s “negligence”.

The deadly inferno , which erupted on the night of January 17 at the mall and took nearly two days to be fully extinguished , had claimed at least 73 lives and left over 1,100 shops in ruins.

A previous charge sheet submitted in July had named six people — including 11-year-old Huzaifa — as the accused. However, a judicial magistrate had rejected the document, noting that the investigating officer (IO) had not conducted a thorough and satisfactory probe.

The fresh charge sheet, dated September 3 and submitted by the Nabi Bux police, names four of those six as the accused sent for trial: Huzaifa’s father Naimatullah who owned an artificial flower shop; Gul Plaza Traders Association President Tanveer Pasta; and association members Ammar Ismail and Muhammad Ramzan.

Meanwhile, regarding the role of authorities, the charge sheet said the fire brigade, Rescue 1122, and Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) “used the resources they had with great efforts to put out the blaze”.

Listing the faults on the building management’s side, the document stated that the Gul Plaza administration lacked adequate tools to extinguish the fire, considering the scale of the building.

It added that there was “no alternative arrangement for emergency lights, due to which people faced difficulties leaving” the building.

It noted that during the investigation, the complainant in the case said only two of the building’s gates were open at the time of the fire. “People could not leave due to the locks on the iron gates,” the charge sheet read.

It went on to say that during the rescue operation, it was discovered that the iron gates on the third floor were padlocked, which “showed that the Gul Plaza administration had their guards close them”.

The document further pointed out that the building management had K-Electric switch off the power supply “despite knowing that they do not have any other alternative arrangement for lighting”.

The charge sheet said Faisal Ibrahim, the owner of Fire Works VIP Service, used to buy the fire safety equipment for the Gul Plaza union.

It added that during the investigation, the quantity of such equipment was found to be inadequate, and that the building management was responsible for repairing and replenishing it. This proved the “criminal negligence and carelessness” of the building management, the charge sheet declared.

It recalled that the findings of the Sindh government’s inquiry commission and the judicial commission also proved the Gul Plaza administration’s negligence. It noted that safety equipment and speakers were not used, while the exits were also found closed.

On the other hand, the charge sheet recalled the rescue operation and the death of a firefighter in the process.

It added, “Due to these reasons, the hard work of the rescue services cannot be doubted, and no concrete testimony emerged during the investigation that would show criminal negligence of rescue authorities.”

The charge sheet highlighted that neither the government inquiry body nor the judicial commission found rescue authorities at fault for any criminal negligence.

While departmental action was taken against Civil Defence Director Abdul Majeed Jagirani and Additional Controller Fatima Memon, “no criminal negligence of the institution was found”, the charge sheet said. It noted that Memon and technical instructor Mirza Mursalin Baig were dismissed from their jobs.

Similarly, the fire brigade’s Station Officer Zaheer Siddiqui was also dismissed from his role, the charge sheet said, adding that no “criminal negligence was found”.

In its report, the Gul Plaza Judicial Commission said the deadly inferno signified a systemic failure across successive provincial and local governments as the legal and administrative mechanisms have existed, but could not be implemented effectively.

Justice Agha Faisal of the Sindh High Court (SHC), who headed the commission, noted that the tragic incident was a grave indictment of the failure of municipal and provincial systems to translate legal duties concerning urban safety into effective protection on the ground.

It stated that the people not only lost their lives to flames, but also due to delay, darkness, locked exits and windows of the ill-fated building, absence of fire safety systems, unimplemented audits/inspections and fragmented authority.

Notably, the commission said KMC, including its fire brigade, Sindh Building Control Authority, Rescue 1122, civil defence department, district administration and others, bore institutional responsibilities for the failure, while material responsibility rested with the people acting as the de facto management of the building together with owners, occupants and commercial operators.

The report was handed over to the provincial government months ago but was released last month, apparently against the backdrop of a tragic hospital fire in Islamabad.

World.title: Eight Pakistan Bar Council members reject proposed changes to council rules
World.content:
Eight members of the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) have rejected proposed amendments seeking to make the council’s proceedings and deliberations confidential, saying the regulatory body of the legal fraternity should instead operate with transparency.

In a letter to the PBC secretary, the eight members — Abid Shahid Zuberi, Muhammad Maqsood Buttar, M Shafqat Mehmood-Chauhan, Munir Ahmed Kakar, Abdul Sattar Khan, Salman Akram Raja, Salahuddin Ahmed and Qazi Muhammad Arshad — said all proceedings of the council should be open, since it was an elected body representing the entire legal fraternity.

“We are not a private club or some secretive government agency,” the two-page letter said. A copy of the letter was also sent to Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Usman Awan, who is the ex-official chairman of the PBC.

The letter emphasised that, as a general rule, all proceedings, deliberations and business of the council should be open and transparent and available for scrutiny by the more than 100,000 lawyers it represented, as well as the public at large.

The PBC intends to amend Rule 97 of the Pakistan Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Rules, 1976, by introducing a new Rule 97-A to provide for the confidentiality and classification of proceedings of the council and its committees.

Under the proposed rule, all acts, proceedings, deliberations and business of the PBC, its committees, tribunals, sub-committees and other bodies constituted under its authority would be treated as confidential and classified. Such information could not be disclosed, communicated, circulated, published or otherwise made available to any person without the express authorisation of the council or the relevant committee.

The proposed amendment also states that no PBC officer, employee, consultant, adviser or any other person with access to the council’s confidential proceedings or records by virtue of their office or functions may disclose, reproduce, transmit, circulate or publish such information, except as otherwise provided under the rules.

The confidentiality under this rule will extend to electronic records, emails, electronic communications, audio or video recordings, digital files, photographs, copies and reproductions of any document or proceedings of the council or its committees, the amendment suggested.

The members recalled that it was also stated in the Sept 4 letter to the members, which was circulated through WhatsApp, that the rules committee had decided that, since the meeting was not being convened shortly, the amendments should be circulated among the members of the PBC under Rule 91 of the Pakistan Legal Practitioners & Bar Councils Rules, 1976, for their views or approval.

The eight members, in their letter, had also drawn the council’s attention to the fact that they had taken strong exception, at the outset, to the manner in which the 1976 rules were sought to be amended, i.e. by way of circular resolution.

Firstly, Rule 91 of the 1976 Rules provides that, “in case of emergency”, the PBC may pass a resolution by way of circulation.

However, neither the secretary nor the rules committee has explained the “emergency” that requires the overnight amendment of the statutory rules, the letter emphasised, adding that circular resolutions were not a substitute for a proper meeting of the PBC, where the merits and demerits of a proposal could be fully discussed and members would have an opportunity to debate and convince each other.

“Unfortunately, there appears to be a trend now in the PBC to pass hugely important and consequential amendments to statutory rules through circular resolutions and bypass the requirement of convening a meeting, even when, clearly, there is no ‘emergency’,” the letter regretted.

Besides, under Rule 91, the rules committee has the power, in case of an emergency, to pass a circular resolution instead of convening a meeting of the rules committee itself. However, it has no power to do so in respect of meetings of the council.

The rules committee is not the convening authority for the full PBC house, nor can it determine when a full PBC meeting is likely to be held, or decide whether any “emergency” exists, the letter highlighted.

The contents of the proposed amendment, however, are even more shocking, the letter stated, as it provides that all acts, proceedings, deliberations and business of the PBC (and any of its committees or other bodies) shall be confidential and classified and shall not be disclosed, circulated or communicated by any PBC member or employee without express permission.

The eight members urged all other members to remember that the council was an elected body and its members were statutory representatives of the entire legal fraternity, rather than a “private club or some secretive government agency”.

“Therefore, all its proceedings, deliberations and business, as a matter of general rule, must be open, transparent and available for the scrutiny of the more than one lakh lawyers we represent, as well as the public at large.”

There may possibly be some limited exceptions to this general rule (for example, in sensitive disciplinary cases involving the privacy of individuals), but the general rule for the PBC must be transparency, the letter emphasised.

“Neither we, personally, nor the PBC, collectively, have anything to hide. Unfortunately, this proposed amendment seeks secrecy as the general rule and disclosure and transparency as the exception,” the letter stated.

The proposed amendment violates the freedom of speech guaranteed under Article 19 of the Constitution and also violates the right to information guaranteed under Article 19-A of the Constitution, the letter highlighted, rejecting the proposed amendments.

World.title: Chinese national rescued from tunnel in Nepal 10 days after catastrophic flooding
World.content:
Rescuers in Nepal pulled a Chinese national alive on Saturday from a tunnel buried by debris, as emergency response teams dug with new vigour in the search for missing people 10 days after catastrophic flooding.

A joint rescue team comprising personnel from the Nepal Army and foreign experts rescued the man from 225 metres inside the tunnel of the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Rasuwa district, a military statement said.

A picture of the rescue published on the army’s Facebook page shows the man, identified only as Luhaitao, with his arms around the shoulders of two camouflage-clad rescuers.

He looked alert but his hands were covered in thick, slimy mud.

“His health is currently being assessed and further search and rescue operations are continuing,” the army said.

The survivor was among hundreds of hydropower workers who went missing since a tsunami-like wall of water and mud swept through the China-Nepal border following a vast glacial and rock collapse on August 26.

Two Nepali hydropower workers were rescued on Friday at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, where searches continued alongside multiple other sites, with at least 12 hydropower projects destroyed by the floods.

So far, 1,344 bodies have been recovered in Nepal, according to the national disaster agency, with around 5,000 people missing.

In China, state media said 31 people had been killed and 531 were missing.

That takes the overall death toll to 1,375 people, and more than 5,500 missing.

Thousands in relief camps

Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP that “work is underway at the tunnels” to locate any survivors.

The government initially said it believed more than 100 workers could be alive inside multiple tunnels.

Rescuers called it a “miracle” after the two Nepali men, caked in mud, were pulled out alive on Friday, nine days after being trapped by the flood.

They were taken to hospital and are said to be in a stable condition.

Experts from India, China, Australia and South Korea have been aiding Nepali rescuers in their search of survivors inside blocked tunnels.

With morgues overflowing, some 1,030 bodies had been buried in mass graves after taking DNA samples for future identification, Nepal Police said on Saturday.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah promised to provide “safe and comfortable accommodation” for thousands of people displaced by the disaster and currently living in temporary relief camps.

“We know that staying there [in camps] is not easy for you,” he said in a Friday post on social media.

But he promised to “once again create an environment where you can dream about and build your future”.

World.title: Asif says devolution of power is 'inevitable', accuses PPP of having contradictory stance on new provinces
World.content:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has said that the devolution of power is “inevitable”, while also accusing the PPP of having a contradictory stance on the issue of new provinces.

“When there is talk of a Saraiki province in Punjab, the PPP supports it or shows a soft corner on this issue. And when there is talk of multiple provinces or administrative units instead of four, talk of ‘Sindhudesh’ begins,” he said in a post on the social media platform X late Friday night.
