World.title: Uzbekistan’s Mirziyoyev to visit Serbia for high-level negotiations
World.content:
Photo: the press service of the Uzbek president

BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 5. Uzbekistan’s President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will pay an official visit to Serbia on September 7–8 at the invitation of Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić to discuss trade, investment, and joint projects in several priority sectors.

This was reflected in the statement by the press service of the Uzbek president.

According to information, Mirziyoyev and Vučić will hold high-level talks in Belgrade, while Uzbek and Serbian officials and business representatives will participate in a bilateral business forum.

The talks will focus on further strengthening the countries’ multifaceted partnership, with particular attention to expanding trade and economic ties and investment cooperation.

The sides are expected to discuss joint projects in transport, mechanical engineering, light and food industries, agriculture, pharmaceuticals and information technology.

“Particular attention will be paid to increasing trade and economic and investment cooperation and implementing joint projects in priority areas,” the presidential press service said.

The agenda will also include cooperation on organized labor migration, as well as efforts to expand interregional and cultural-humanitarian ties.

The planned business forum is expected to provide an additional platform for companies from Uzbekistan and Serbia to identify investment opportunities and develop direct business contacts, particularly in sectors targeted for joint projects.

The visit comes as Uzbekistan continues to expand economic and investment partnerships with European countries, while seeking to diversify trade, attract foreign capital and develop industrial cooperation.

A substantial package of intergovernmental and interagency agreements is expected to be signed following the summit, according to the presidential press service.

The agreements are expected to provide a framework for advancing cooperation across economic, investment, labor, regional and cultural areas and translating the two countries’ political dialogue into concrete projects.

World.title: Russia to halt strikes on Kyiv during US diplomatic talks
World.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has ordered a halt in strikes against Ukraine's capital Kyiv during a US envoy visit to the region.

US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on Saturday, local time, to revive a stalled push to end Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

A motorcade, carrying Mr Witkoff, Mr Kushner and Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev Dmitriev, left Moscow's governmental airport and headed towards the city.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Ukraine would halt air-strikes during the envoys' trip and urged Moscow to do the same.

Mr Putin later responded with an order to halt strikes against Kyiv for three days, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russia's Tass news agency Saturday.



He said the pause would begin at midnight local time, adding that the decision was tied to preparations for the American delegation's visit to Kyiv the following day.

US envoy upon their arrival at Vnukovo International Airport in Moscow, Russia, September 5, 2026. (via Reuters)

Ahead of the envoy this week, US President Donald Trump said the United States had a fresh concrete proposal aimed at ending the war, which is now in its fifth year.

He did not, however, elaborate on what that proposal would be.

Aerial attacks escalate

While the two sides have agreed to this focused ceasefire as diplomatic talks take place, August has seen deadly strikes across Ukraine and Russia.

Ukraine's drone strikes on Russian oil refineries have led to a summer of fuel shortages and rising prices for Russian motorists, while some 30 attacks on giant warehouses belonging mostly to Wildberries, Russia's biggest online retailer, have affected the consumer economy.

Russian drone attack hits Ukraine's SBU headquarters in Kyiv on Friday — the 10th consecutive day of heavy attacks on the capital — and Mr Zelenskyy vowed to retaliate.

Most recently, Russian attacks killed five people and wounded five more at an industrial facility in Ukraine's southern Dnipropetrovsk region, local military administration head Oleksandr Hanzha said.

He described those killed as employees at the site.

"A locksmith, an electrician, a plumber and a machinist. People of peaceful professions. They were simply working their shift. They were doing their job when enemy missiles cut off their lives," he said.

Zelenskyy links Russian strikes to envoys' visit

The air war between Russia and Ukraine has intensified as troops have struggled to make progress along the 1,250-kilometre front line.

Drones make life in Russia's cities a 'nightmare' For years, people in Russia's largest and most affluent cities were shielded from the impacts of their country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, but not anymore.

Russia has recently been using fast-flying, jet-powered drones, and the recurring wail of air-raid sirens has become part of daily life in Kyiv.

In a social media post on Saturday, Mr Zelenskyy said Russia had carried out overnight strikes on Kyiv and Boryspil international airports, and linked the attack to the planned US visit.

"Clearly, these Russian strikes on the airports are a reaction to the discussions and preparations for the possibility of the US side using an aircraft to travel to Ukraine," he said.

"We have taken note of this Russian move, and next week we will adjust our operation accordingly regarding Russian airspace, which has become dangerous because of our drones and missiles in the sky.

" Of course, there are and will be no threats to diplomacy from our side. "

Negotiations stalled by US-Iran war

The last known visit to Moscow by Mr Witkoff and Mr Kushner, who is President Donald Trump's son-in-law, was in January 2026, when they met Mr Putin in the Kremlin.

They have never visited Kyiv, but Mr Zelenskyy said he was expecting them in the Ukrainian capital on Sunday.

Washington's push to end the fighting has lost momentum as US attention has been focused for the last six months on its war with Iran.

Earlier in the week, Mr Putin had described negotiations as "to a certain extent frozen".

AP/Reuters

World.title: 2,000 cases of suspected food poisoning from Indonesia's free school meals
World.content:
Nearly 2,000 people have fallen ill in suspected food poisoning outbreaks linked to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto 's flagship Free Nutritious Meals program this week.

The cases have raised fresh concerns over the food safety of the program as the government rapidly expands the multi-billion-dollar initiative nationwide, officials said on Saturday.

The incidents, reported between Tuesday and Thursday in East Java, Central Java, West Sumatra, Aceh and South Sulawesi, affected about 1,950 students, teachers and Islamic boarding school pupils who became sick after consuming meals distributed under the government program, known by its Indonesian abbreviation MBG.

The outbreaks are the latest setback for Prabowo's signature free-meals program, which has been rolled out across the archipelago despite repeated food poisoning incidents and corruption allegations.

Two girls eating free school meals at a school in Jakarta, Indonesia, November 2025. (ABC News: Tim Swanston)

The largest outbreak was reported in Central Java's Rembang regency, where 752 students and 25 teachers at State Senior High School 1 Lasem suffered diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting and stomach pain after eating meals provided through the program, according to Rembang Health Office head Ali Syofi'i.

In Sidoarjo, East Java, 730 people, most of them students at the Manbaul Hikam Islamic boarding school, were affected in another suspected food poisoning incident linked to the program.

The free lunches that caused food poisoning Despite thousands of cases of food poisoning, Indonesia's government intends to expand a controversial program giving schoolchildren free meals.

Sidoarjo health office chief Lakhsmie Herawati Yuwantina said 706 victims had been discharged and were recovering at home.

Authorities also reported 276 suspected cases involving students and teachers in Agam regency, West Sumatra, where food distribution from the local nutrition service centre was suspended pending an investigation.

In Aceh's Bener Meriah regency, 15 elementary school students and a school principal were treated after experiencing dizziness, nausea and other symptoms following a school meal.

Another 152 students from two junior high schools in Tana Toraja, South Sulawesi, were treated at three hospitals after developing symptoms consistent with food poisoning.

No deaths have been reported, and authorities are investigating the causes of the outbreaks.

Plagued by controversy

The latest incidents add to a growing number of food poisoning cases linked to the program since its launch in January 2025.

According to health ministry surveillance data as of September 2, food poisoning incidents associated with MBG have affected 50,059 people in 560 cases across 245 districts and cities in 36 provinces.

Ex-head of Indonesian school meals linked to food poisoning arrested The ex-chief of Indonesia's free school meals program linked to food poisoning cases has been arrested after a corruption probe.

In a hearing with the House's Commission IX overseeing health issues, National Nutrition Agency chief Sudaryono said internal reviews found that roughly 80 to 90 per cent of previous food poisoning incidents were linked to failures to follow food safety procedures, including rules governing food storage, receipt of ingredients, temperature control and consumption deadlines.

"The recent incidents in Sidoarjo, Agam, Rembang and other areas have been a major blow for us," Sudaryono said.

He said the agency was tightening oversight of meal providers and reviewing about 27,000 meal distribution centres nationwide.

A woman protesting against Indonesia's free school meals program outside the headquarters of the National Nutrition Agency in November 2025. (ABC News: Tim Swanston)

Inspectors have found hundreds of allegedly fictitious facilities, while at least 833 kitchens have been shut down for failing to meet hygiene and sanitation standards.

In June, the former head of the program, Dadan Hindayana, was arrested by the Attorney General's Office following an investigation into alleged corruption.

The free meals program aims to combat malnutrition and reduce childhood stunting by providing meals to nearly 90 million students, toddlers and pregnant women.

The initiative, expected to cost about $28 billion through 2029, is a cornerstone of Prabowo's administration and one of his key campaign promises.

AP

World.title: Engine flames from Sydney-bound Qantas flight forces plane to be diverted
World.content:
A Sydney-bound Qantas flight from Queenstown in New Zealand has been forced to divert as footage taken shortly after take-off appears to show flames shooting out from one side of the plane.

A spokesperson for the airline confirmed flight QF122 from Queenstown had experienced an incident mid-flight on Saturday, saying it was a "suspected engine issue", and had to be diverted.

"One of our flights to Sydney experienced a suspected engine issue after take-off from Queenstown this afternoon and the aircraft diverted to Christchurch," they said.

"Our pilots are highly trained to manage situations like this and the aircraft landed safely."

In footage provided to ABC News, the aircraft's left engine seems to be emitting flames.

Fight QF122 from Queenstown was due to land in Sydney at 4:50pm on Saturday. (Supplied: Liam Aspinall)

The Boeing aircraft had left the alpine ski town just before 3:30pm and was scheduled to land at Kingsford Smith Airport at 4:50pm.

The national carrier told the ABC that the aircraft was cleared for a priority landing at Christchurch, and both engines remained operating throughout, with no engine shutdown or failure experienced.

Liam Aspinall was sitting with friends having a drink in Queenstown when he noticed the flames approaching from a distance.

"I noticed flames appearing to come off the thing as it was approaching us from afar," Mr Aspinall told ABC News.

" Sounded like gunshots, [it] was loud. "

Support is being provided to passengers, according to the Qantas spokesperson, in recognition of what "would have been a distressing experience".

Passengers are being offered accommodation and help with getting alternative flights.

World.title: Two briefly detained over 'chaotic scenes' at Canberra junior AFL match
World.content:
Two people were briefly taken into custody at a junior AFL grand final in Canberra last night after reports of flares being set off and items thrown at players.

Officers were called to Phillip Oval around 8:30pm after receiving reports of a disturbance during the Under 18s AFL Canberra Grand Final between Marist College and the Belconnen Magpies.

"Reports received by police were that from a group of between 50 and 75 teens, items had been thrown at players, flares had been discharged, and multiple patrons were intoxicated," ACT Policing said in a statement.

"Two people were briefly taken into custody and released at the venue."

'Chaotic scenes' at conclusion of the match

Marist College deputy principal Liam Stakelum says the spectators briefly taken into custody were part of a group that displayed poor behaviour throughout the match. (Facebook: Marist College Canberra)

In a message to parents of Marist AFL players, the college's deputy principal Liam Stakelum said the end of the game was "chaotic", with spectators taken into custody for "anti-social behaviour".

"They were part of a group that exhibited considerably poor behaviour throughout the match," Mr Stakelum said.

"After [quarter] time, we made the decision to keep our students down one end to ensure they were safe and away from the potential risk.

" I will state that it does not look like these [spectators] were affiliated with Belconnen. "

ACT Policing said after the match concluded, event management staff advised all spectators to clear the venue.

"All patrons left the scene without further incident," the ACT Policing statement said.

ACT Policing confirmed two people were taken into custody before being released at the venue a short time later. (ABC News: Ian Cutmore)

Mr Stakelum said in his message to parents that officers believed the group posed a risk to students, and wanted to limit their engagement with the group as much as possible.

"I know the chaotic scenes at the conclusion of the match are hard to reconcile, but I do want everyone to know that the police were the ones who were in control," he said.

"The decision to remove everyone from the ground again was [made by] the police.

"This was done because they couldn't differentiate between the true Belconnen supporters, and the spectators who were causing the trouble.

"We may not agree with the decision, but coming from a safety perspective, I can understand the intent. Scenarios like this are not easy to manage."

An AFL spokesperson said the league worked closely with police to contain the situation and ensure the safe conduct of the game. (ABC News: Daniel Miles)

An AFL spokesperson said the safety of players, officials and spectators was "of paramount importance" to the AFL.

"[Safety] guided all decision-making during last night's U18s boys' grand final," the spokesperson said.

"The AFL worked closely with ACT Policing throughout the event and took appropriate steps to contain the situation and ensure the safe conduct of the match."

The Belconnen Magpies Football Club has been contacted for comment.

World.title: Five children in hospital after strong winds pick up two jumping castles
World.content:
Five children have been taken to hospital after jumping castles were picked up by winds in two separate incidents, in Victoria and New South Wales, on one day.

In Banksia, in Sydney's south, NSW Ambulance treated a boy and a girl for head injuries about 1pm, before taking them to Sydney Children's Hospital in a stable condition.

An infant with minor injuries was also hospitalised, and a woman was treated at the scene.

Just hours earlier, in Victoria's south-west, two children were taken to hospital after a jumping castle was lifted into the air, at a birthday party.

Victoria Police said the incident took place at a home in Lower Duneed Road in Mount Duneed, near Geelong, shortly before 11am.

"Two children were thrown from the jumping castle and taken to hospital by road," a spokesperson said.

"A large number of other children also playing on the jumping castle at the time escaped injury."

Ambulance Victoria said a mobile intensive care ambulance and advanced life support paramedics attended the scene.

"Two primary-school-aged children were transported to Geelong University Hospital, a boy and a girl both with upper body injuries in stable conditions," it said in a statement.



In December 2021, six children died and three others were seriously injured after a freak wind lifted a jumping castle into the air at a primary school in Devonport, Tasmania.

A coronial inquest into the Hillcrest tragedy will begin later this month.

World.title: Peter Katsambanis remembered as one of Liberal Party's 'finest' warriors
World.content:
Former MP Peter Katsambanis has been remembered as one of the Liberal Party's "fiercest and finest" warriors following his death, aged 60.

Mr Katsambanis served in the parliaments of Western Australia and Victoria, and was a prominent Greek Australian.

His wife Karalee Katsambanis said his family was "devastated" by his death.

"He was a great man: loved, adored, treasured and respected by so many people," she wrote in a tribute on social media.

"As his wife, I've lost my soulmate and love of my life and I thank everyone for all their support."

She also thanked the heart transplant team at The Alfred hospital who had been caring for him.

Peter Katsambanis is being remembered as the "fiercest and finest of warriors" for the Liberal Party's cause. (ABC News: Jessica Warriner)

Mr Katsambanis served in the WA parliament from 2013 to 2021, first in the Legislative Council and then in the Legislative Assembly as the member for Hillarys.

The seat had been a Liberal heartland before Mr Katsambanis was defeated by Caitlin Collins in Labor's landslide victory in the 2021 state election.

He had held the positions of opposition spokesperson for police, road safety, justice and industrial relations.

He was also a member of the Victorian parliament, from 1996 to 2002.

Liberals mourn loss

The Liberal Party of WA's state director Simon Morgan said Mr Katsambanis would be sorely missed.

"Peter Katsambanis was the fiercest and finest of warriors for the Liberal cause as a student, a trusted adviser and as a member of parliament in both Victoria and Western Australia," Mr Morgan said.

"Our party is poorer for his loss and we extend our heartfelt sympathies to Karalee and to all of Peter's children at this sad time."

Liberal Peter Katsambanis faces 'big challenge' to retain Hillarys Peter Katsambanis is facing a ''big challenge'' to prevent Labor's Caitlin Collins from wresting Hillarys from the Liberals.

WA Opposition Leader Basil Zempilas said Mr Katsambanis made an incredible contribution to the Liberal Party and to public life in two states.

"Service always came first for Peter, he was such a committed representative and he occupies a rare place in Australian politics, having served in the Victorian parliament and in both houses of the parliament of Western Australia," Mr Zempilas said.

"He will be greatly missed by his friends and former colleagues and we extend our very sincere condolences to Karalee and all the family."

Mr Zempilas also acknowledged his "significant contribution" to the Greek Australian community.

Mr Katsambanis served as president of the World Hellenic Inter-Parliamentary Association from 2017 to 2021.

He was also a vice-president of the Hellenic Community of Western Australia.

His family will provided details in the coming days for his funeral, which will be held in Melbourne.

World.title: Man on run after allegedly attacking three people with axe
World.content:
A man believed to be wielding an axe has allegedly attacked three people, including an elderly man and woman, in Gippsland and remains on the run, say Victoria Police.

Police were told the man, who is known to the victims, allegedly attacked the pair and another man at an address in Cowies Road, Tyers, about 12:30pm today.

The man, in his 50s, fled the address and the victims were able to call emergency services for help.

The elderly male and the second man were airlifted to hospital in Melbourne with life-threatening injuries, police said in a statement.

"The elderly woman also sustained critical injuries and was taken to hospital."

Police said a large-scale search was underway for the alleged offender, whom they believe may be armed with an axe and a handsaw.

He was last seen wearing a black-and-mustard-coloured jacket and carrying a black backpack.

Police said anyone who sees the man should not approach him, and instead contact Triple Zero (000).

Anyone with information has been urged to contact Crime Stoppers via 1800 333 000 or www.crimestoppersvic.com.au.

World.title: AFLW wrap: Suns rally after coaching spray, Roos maintain historic run
World.content:
Daisy D'Arcy has produced a dazzling display as Gold Coast's band of youngsters posted a three-point AFLW victory over Port Adelaide in a three-goal thriller.

D'Arcy racked up 34 disposals and 694m gained as the Suns, featuring nine first-year players, posted their second win of the season with a 2.5 (17) to 1.8 (14) victory.

Gemma Houghton scored Port Adelaide's only goal of the match at the 9-minute mark of the opening quarter, with the Power held to just six behinds for the rest of the match.

Sunny Lapin scored Gold Coast's first goal in the opening term with a nice effort on the run, but the Suns trailed until Havana Harris kicked truly at the 11-minute mark of the third quarter.

It would prove to be the match-winning goal, with neither side able to score a major in the final term as the blustery conditions took their toll.

Port had one final chance to win the match with 30 seconds remaining, but Gold Coast was able to spoil what looked set to be a certain mark.

D'Arcy was the standout player, but she received plenty of help from Niamh McLaughlin (24 disposals) and Charlie Rowbottom (22 disposals, 11 tackles).

Suns coach Rhyce Shaw gave a rare blast at quarter-time, and his side responded by scraping out the gritty win.

"We copped a spray, but that's what we need sometimes," D'Arcy told Fox Footy.

"The message was to go out and play our game of footy. Obviously the weather conditions meant it was going to be scrappy.

"The spray was to put our head down and get to it. I thought we did that well. I'm super proud of the girls to get the win and put the head down."

Abbey Dowrick racked up seven clearances from 15 disposals for Port, while Maria Moloney finished with 17 disposals, four clearances and 10 tackles.

The Power's Matilda Scholz was a force in the ruck with 15 disposals and 20 hitouts.

The result left both Gold Coast and Port with 2-2 records.

McDonald fires late as Bulldogs surge to stun Swans

Three final-quarter goals from young forward Emma McDonald inspired the Western Bulldogs to a soaring 27-point win over Sydney.

Emma McDonald kicked three goals in the final quarter to guide the Bulldogs to victory. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Jonathan DiMaggio)

Down by four points at three-quarter time, the Bulldogs surged home with the breeze by kicking five unanswered goals at the Whitten Oval to win 9.6 (60) to 5.3 (33).

After two behinds in the first three quarters, McDonald starred with three goals in the final term in a coming-of-age performance.

Rylie Wilcox also added a major in the last quarter to finish with three goals in a best-on-ground performance.

Runner-up in the last two Bulldogs' best-and-fairest counts, Wilcox had a game-high 26 disposals to go with her game-changing day in front of goal.

Coming off a thrashing by relentless back-to-back premiers North Melbourne, the Bulldogs had to overcome a burst from Swans superstar Chloe Molloy.

Down at half-time, the Swans hit the lead in the third term thanks to two goals from Molloy.

It was Sydney's first defeat of the season after it opened its campaign with big wins over Adelaide, Essendon and St Kilda.

But injuries have started to catch up with the Swans, who are missing high-profile recruit Taylor Smith for at least another two games.

Champion Kangaroos belt St Kilda

The all-conquering North Melbourne destroyed struggling St Kilda by 92 points for a record-extending 31st-consecutive victory.

The winless Saints registered the first behind of the match, but North predictably stepped up after that to win 14.15 (99) to 1.1 (7)

Having not lost since the 2023 grand final, the Kangaroos predictably condemned St Kilda to a fourth-straight defeat to open their season that will heap further pressure on coach Nick Dal Santo.

North spearhead Tahlia Randall starred with five goals, three coming in a second-half onslaught.

Veteran forward Kate Shierlaw finished with four goals, firing early with three in the first half.

Midfield maestros Ash Riddell (39 possessions, one goal) and Jasmine Garner (38, 11 clearances) were typically prolific, helping the Kangaroos dominate the clearances.

Ash Richards was St Kilda's sole goal-kicker, coming in the second quarter.

Lions beat GWS

In the final game of the day, the Brisbane Lions had a 31-point win over GWS at Ipswich.

Shanae Davidson kicked two for the Lions, as they ran out winners by 7.13 (55) to 3.6 (24).

The win keeps the Lions on the fringe of the top eight, behind eighth-placed Richmond on percentage.

AAP

World.title: Adelaide v Western Bulldogs player ratings: Beveridge’s men were down and out. These guns made a game of it
World.content:
SportAFLAFL 2026 Opinion Adelaide v Western Bulldogs player ratings: Beveridge’s men were down and out. These guns made a game of it Jon Pierik Sports journalist for The Age September 5, 2026 — 10:45pm

September 5, 2026 — 10:45pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Loading

After doing it the hard way, through a wildcard final win over Collingwood at the MCG last week, The Bulldogs were right up against it at Adelaide Oval. But no one should ever write-off Luke Beveridge’s men and their never-say-die spirit. The Dogs charged to a one-point lead in the final term. But Adelaide, courtesy of their firepower up forward, responded in style – winning by 22 points in front of more than 51,000 screaming fans. Jon Pierik runs his eye over every player in this elimination final. Marcus Bontempelli leads the Bulldogs off the field for the final time in 2026. AFL Photos via Getty Images



Western Bulldogs (3) Cody Weightman: The flashy small forward had an early set shot snap from the boundary, but went to ground too often in the first term. While his endeavour could not be questioned, he needed to do better to negate opponent Josh Worrell, who was arguably best afield. 3/10 (4) Marcus Bontempelli: Branded “the best Bulldog ever” by club great Brad Johnson during Kayo Sports’ pre-game coverage, the man dubbed “the Rolls Royce” did all he could to will his team over the line, finishing with 27 touches and 10 clearances. He began quietly with just the five first-term touches, but got moving in the second, finding himself more goal-side. He was sent forward in the third, but injected himself more into the midfield in the final term, delivering run and carry. 7.5/10



(6) Cooper Hynes: The strong-bodied forward-midfielder was prolific early with 15 disposals and 318 metres gained to half-time. He continued to work hard, and was steady when the contest was there to be won. 6.5/10 (7) Rory Lobb: The veteran defender looked lost up forward against Collingwood last week, and was sent to defence on Riley Thilthorpe, where he was excellent until the final break when the burly Crow got busy. That wasn’t just on him though, for the Crows lifted through the midfield. 7/10 (9) Ryley Sanders: The exciting midfielder won’t want to watch this game again. He was another who struggled to get going early, having just the five touches before half-time, and finished with only 10 disposals. Needed to lift after the main break, but had a nightmare moment early in the third term when he dropped the ball, leading to an Izak Rankine goal. 3/10 View post on X (14) Rhylee West: Typically a goal-kicking forward, the son-of-a-gun was injected into the midfield in a brilliant move by Luke Beveridge. He was arguably best afield in the first half with 12 touches, including five clearances, but faded as the evening progressed. 6.5/10



(18) James O’Donnell: The reliable defender had the job on Taylor Walker, and was at his intercept-marking best early. But “Big Tex” lifted late, as all great forwards do. 6.5/10 (19) Connor Budarick: The versatile small defender worked hard but did not have a major impact. 5/10 View post on X (20) Ed Richards: The dashing midfielder snapped the Dogs’ opening goal, the visitors rewarded for multiple inside-50 entries. World.title: Two children hurt when thrown from jumping castle lifted into air by wind
World.content:
Two children were injured when a jumping castle was swept into the air by high winds at a party near Geelong on Saturday morning. The children were thrown from the jumping castle around 11am and taken to hospital, and are in stable condition. Two of the children were left with upper-body injuries. Nine News Paramedics and police rushed to the house on Lower Duneed Road in Mount Duneed, and police said “a large number of other children also playing on the jumping castle at the time escaped injury”. Ambulance Victoria confirmed “two primary school aged children” were taken to Geelong University Hospital with injuries to their upper bodies in a stable condition.



The incident has revived memories of the tragedy in Hillcrest, Tasmania, in 2021, when six children died after a jumping castle at a primary school fete was lifted into the air and thrown 75 metres by a “mini tornado” during a freak weather event. Three young children were also taken to hospital after powerful winds lifted a jumping castle into the air in Sydney, as wild weather caused widespread power outages in the city’s west and left more than 90,000 households without electricity. Three children were injured when a jumping castle became airborne in Banksia, in Sydney’s south, amid ferocious wind gusts on Saturday. Nine News Ausgrid confirmed about 40,000 customers had been left in the dark, as swaths of Sydney’s west suffered outages after high winds damaged one of the company’s substations. Another 50,000 customers on Endeavour Energy’s network were also without power. The outages came after a cool change ripped through NSW, with gusts of wind surpassing 80km/h recorded at Sydney Airport late on Saturday afternoon. The temperature in Sydney had hovered about 30 degrees, accompanied by strong north-westerly winds.



Emergency services were called to Gardiner Park in Banksia, about 12 kilometres south of Sydney’s CBD, about 1.20pm on Saturday after the jumping castle became airborne, a NSW Ambulance spokeswoman said. The children were taken to Sydney Children’s Hospital after being treated by paramedics at the scene. A preschool-aged boy and girl suffered head injuries, while a baby was treated for minor injuries. A woman was also taken to hospital with minor injuries, the spokeswoman said. All three children were in a stable condition. Be the first to know when major news happens.

World.title: ‘Survivable pockets’: Australian tunnel expert arrives in Nepal, hopeful of more rescues
World.content:
WorldAsiaFloods ‘Survivable pockets’: Australian tunnel expert arrives in Nepal, hopeful of more rescues Michael McGowan Updated September 5, 2026 — 9:55pm ,first published 4:50pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Kathmandu: An Australian tunnelling expert who helped to orchestrate the extraordinary rescue of two workers from a hydropower tunnel in northern Nepal is headed for the disaster zone, firmly believing there is still hope of finding more survivors trapped hundreds of metres below the earth. After helping to lead the rescue operation remotely from his home in Victoria this week, engineer and geologist Arnold Dix flew into Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu, late on Friday night (Nepal time). Australian tunnelling expert Arnold Dix has arrived in disaster-stricken Nepal believing there is still hope of finding survivors. Justin McManus It comes as rescuers in Nepal pulled a Chinese national alive from a hydropower tunnel on Saturday, according to a social media post by the country’s prime minister’s office, and in a separate effort, rescuers pulled a woman out alive from a house 10 days after floods hit Nuwakot town, a Nepalese army spokesperson said. The latest tunnel rescue brings the total to three workers pulled alive from the Trishuli hydropower project. Two Nepalese workers were rescued from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower plant on Friday.



Nepal’s army said a joint team of Nepalese military personnel and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre tunnel, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. In flood-hit Nuwakot town, a woman was rescued alive from a house, Nepal’s army spokesperson said Saturday. Officials said she was airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment. Loading Images released by Nepal’s army showed rescuers finding the woman covered in mud inside the damaged house. They gave her bottled water before pulling her to safety, wrapped in a gray blanket. While the odds are against Dix and the rest of the global team of experts providing advice to Nepalese authorities on the ongoing rescue mission, he said that he absolutely believed there was hope of finding more survivors under the earth some 10 days after the devastating floods.



“In the game of paper, scissor, rock, human, the odds aren’t good. But yeah [there are] survivable pockets, absolutely, and that’s what we’re aiming for,” he said. On Saturday morning, he boarded a helicopter for the Chilime Hydropower Plant, high in the Himalayan valley and close to the Chinese border. There he will meet with members of the Indian rescue team he worked with after 41 men were trapped in the Silkyara Bend-Barkot tunnel in the Himalayas in 2023. Dix has also worked on other rescue missions, including at Ground Zero after September 11. “We’re just like the underground rescue buddies,” he told this masthead just ahead of his flight on Saturday. A helicopter drops search and rescue teams at the exit tunnel of the Chilime Hydropower Plant during the week. Kate Geraghty



It has been more than a week since devastating floods tore through Nepal, causing tsunami-like waves of water, rock and debris that has resulted in 1294 confirmed deaths. More than 5000 people are still missing, including 583 foreign nationals. The Chinese government has reported 31 confirmed deaths and 531 missing – including 261 foreign nationals – on the Tibet side of the border. Related Article Floods At first, the smell is overwhelming. Then, they open the book of the dead Among those still unaccounted for are workers believed to be trapped inside the hydropower tunnels that Nepal has used to harness the fast-flowing waters of the Himalayas and increase the blackout-prone country’s power generation. Nepal’s Independent Power Producers’ Association said during the week that it believed ​at least eight people could be trapped in the Chilime tunnel. It is one of seven hydropower tunnels at which rescue operations are taking place, with hundreds of workers believed to have been trapped. Until Friday, Dix had helped the effort remotely from Australia, unable to board a plane during the crucial hours and days after the disaster.



“Time was of the essence,” he said. “I couldn’t lose two days because I knew they had to start digging.” They had focused on the Trishuli 3A ­hydropower project, and he said the rescue of mechanical foreman Sanjay Sah and mechanical supervisor Kabir Maharjan from the tunnel on Friday was confirmation of the work he and others had been doing throughout the week. “[It means] we’ve got survivable zones in there,” Dix said. “That confirms our theory, if you like. Until that, it was a theory. We really didn’t know if it was survivable in there.” It makes him believe there could “absolutely” be more workers still alive inside. “Of course, the odds are against us. Like, you wouldn’t, you know, go to the casino and play the house on these things normally,” he said.



Dix and his team had relied on engineering drawings of the massive hydropower structures that Nepal uses to generate electricity, as well as satellite imagery, to identify the survivable pockets inside. “The world has never had something like this,” he said. Arnold Dix has previously helped to orchestrate the rescue of 41 Indian workers who were trapped for 17 days after a landslide in the Himalayas. “We’re not dealing with tunnels that might’ve collapsed. They won’t have. We’re dealing with tunnels that are filled up with stuff. “It’s this explosive inrush. It just turns the textbook on its head … that’s why the rescue yesterday was so important because we’ve never dealt with anything like this.”



While they were confident in their theory, the challenge of digging into the deep, unstable earth, where “rocks the size of cars” had barrelled into the tunnels, presented many challenges of its own. Related Article Floods In Nepal, hope gives way to grief. Few are counting on miracles “That’s on the one hand, and the other hand, [the question was] how the hell are we going to get in there to get them?” he said. “You have to find a reason to use your resources, which is where might people be alive? That’s the first question, and then your second question is, ‘OK, now, how do we get them?’ “You can’t just dig everywhere. You’ve seen the destruction here, so you’ve got to be very specific in what you do.”

World.title: Two sin bins and a last-minute match-winner: Cronulla’s season continues to slip
World.content:
SportNRLNRL 2026 Two sin bins and a last-minute match-winner: Cronulla’s season continues to slip Billie Eder September 5, 2026 — 9:47pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

So long as Cronulla escaped Saturday night without any injuries or suspensions, they could have considered it a win, regardless of the score. But that’s not what happened. Instead, the Sharks went into the 79th minute of the match ahead on the scoreboard, despite having two men sent to the bin in the opening 10 minutes, before a Harry Grant flick pass to Trent Loiero clawed back victory for Melbourne on the siren, 24-20. Loading To say it was a deflating end for the Cronulla faithful inside Shark Park would be an understatement.



Now, the Sharks head into their elimination final against the Cowboys next Saturday on a two-game losing streak, after an embarrassing loss to Parramatta which squandered their chance of a top-four finish and resulted in coach Craig Fitzgibbon taking his frustrations out on a computer monitor. Fitzgibbon was unhappy again after the match. But not for losing the game – for the officiating of referee Todd Smith who called 18 infringements in the first half alone, and for both of Melbourne’s opening tries. Hugo Peel’s opener came from a forward pass and the second from Sua Fa’alogo appeared to be grounded on the dead-ball line. Sua Faalogo scores Melbourne’s second try of the night. Getty Images “You’ve been around as long as I have. If you don’t know what a forward pass looks like at this point of your career, I don’t know either,” Fitzgibbon said to reporters. The positive for Cronulla is they get their star players back next week, with Nicho Hynes, Braydon Trindall, Blayke Brailey and KL Iro all having been rested against Melbourne.



It’s fair to say Cronulla will need far more convincing and consistent performances if they hope to contend for the premiership a decade after the club lifted the trophy for the first and only time. The Sharks will start as favourites for their clash against the Cowboys, but it will be Trindall’s first game back after three weeks off following a shoulder injury, and the match will likely be held at the more neutral venue of Allianz Stadium rather than their beloved ‘Shark Park’. Saturday was anything but reassuring for Cronulla fans after Melbourne stormed to a 12-0 lead following the double sin-binning. Debutant Michael Gabrael was sent to the bin in the fifth minute of the match – and the first tackle of his NRL career – for a shoulder charge on Siulagi Tuimalatu-Brown.



Siulagi Tuimalatu-Brown was eventually stretchered off and taken to hospital. Getty Images The Melbourne winger was stretchered off and taken to hospital for a precautionary check after experiencing neck pain. Then Ronaldo Mulitalo left Cronulla with only 11 men on the field after he was also sent to the bin for striking Melbourne hooker Harry Grant in a melee. Despite the brain snap, Multialo should also be available for selection next week. However, Cronulla will have to wait for the match review committee’s verdict on a possible hip-drop tackle by Addin Fonua-Blake on Cooper Clarke.



Cronulla celebrate Billy Burns try. Getty Images The Sharks fought to get back into the contest and went into the sheds ahead 18-12 at half-time after tries to Sione Katoa, Riley Jones and Billy Burns. Related Article NRL 2026 Warriors pip Manly to give Penrith minor premiership edge; new No.7 shines for Raiders Cronulla’s comeback coincided with Melbourne halfback Jarhome Hughes succumbing to a hamstring injury – a concern for the Kiwis with World Cup selection around the corner. The Sharks appeared to have the match sealed up with a penalty goal from Niwhai Puru the difference between the sides heading into the final minute of the game.



But Melbourne’s never-say-die trio of Cameron Munster, Grant and Sua Fa’alogo managed to find a spark in the final minute of the match to set up Loiero’s try and save Craig Bellamy the embarrassment of his worst win-loss ratio since the 2002 season. World.title: From break point to empathy
World.content:
Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

The tussle over the Naremburn tennis courts between the Northern Suburbs Tennis Association and the Metropolitan Local Aboriginal Land Council (“Game, set, match: Players face eviction in tennis stoush”, August 30) has provided Willoughby MP Tim James with the opportunity to make perhaps the most ironic statement of all. James says it “doesn’t sit right” with him that local tennis players are being “forced out of a site it’s occupied for more than 40 years”. Mmmm … Margie Christowski, Roseville Say goodbye to the good old days Getty Images The irony of an Aboriginal Land Council evicting a group of white upper-middle-class tennis players from their stolen lands has been worth living 73 years to see. Wow. “It’s not just about the social interaction.” Really? Now you might understand just a fraction of the pain that the first six generations of European Australians inflicted so casually and criminally on Indigenous Australians when stealing their lands. Suck it up, Northern Suburbs Tennis Association, and move on like you expected Indigenous Australians to do, and know this, as the census will reveal: the number of Indigenous Australians continues now to grow decade after decade, in their country. They are back. Jim Pearce, Oak Flats “It doesn’t sit right with me that a community asset that has served generations of local families is being forced out of a site it’s occupied for more than 40 years,” says Willoughby MP Tim James. I totally understand and agree with those sentiments, Mr James. Hang on – 40 years? Now I’m confused. Obviously, you must have said 60,000 years, but were misquoted. Susan Newman, Mona Vale Love and marriage Your correspondent (Letters, August 30) is unwittingly victim blaming. Most families have two parents, and rather than blaming a “submissive” wife who has been coerced by society into valuing beauty and money, look to her partner with “inappropriate behaviour” who chose her. It’s time that men took responsibility for their actions and attitudes, and those of their associates. Not “look what you made me do”. And while mothers do greatly influence their children’s behaviour, they need to do so in an environment of respect and equality, while fathers need to be good role models. Rowan Godwin, Rozelle PM’s hot mess



Paul Sakkal (“PM pivots to positivity to counter Hanson”, August 30) failed to mention that the major reason that Labor supporters are disappointed with Anthony Albanese is the continual approval of new coal mines that are worsening the future of the world, despite warnings from scientists and the obvious effects on food supply of the heating of the oceans, melting ice in the Himalayas and Antarctica. Much of the press seems to be collaborating with political leaders everywhere in highlighting distractions – immigration, tariffs, etc – rather than the most important issue of counteracting global warming. Colin Sutton, Newtown All shoulders to weal At a time when the Labor government is under fire for inaction, I have a suggestion that may be helpful. Why don’t we use the Bathla debacle (“‘Contagion’ fears after $3.3b Bathla collapse”, August 30) as an opportunity for our very wealthy, secure national superannuation industry to intervene and ensure the completion of all properties and payment of debts? Their members would become shareholders in the interest of public security and future support. What an excellent example of government action in full view of voters. People before profits. Public funding, as investors, replacing private greed and failure. There has been so much bragging about billion-dollar profit results, at a time when Australians are battling cost-of-living pressures, that one wonders why more of the wealth could not have been shared with customers and suppliers rather than shareholders and chief executives. Come on, Albo, here’s your chance to shine. John Robertson, Springwood The collapse of the Bathla group will probably give rise to criticism of Labor’s changes to the property market. The real problem is that rational first home buyers can’t afford to get into the property market. They will just have to pay the maximum rent that property investors can gather. There goes first home buyers’ capacity to save for a mortgage. A correction is needed. John Rome, Mount Lawley Given the housing shortage and the work partially completed by Bathla group, isn’t it in the interest of the state, the country, the people investing in partly finished homes and the workers involved that either state or federal governments, or both, take over and get the jobs finished? It would be a win-win for all involved. Don Leayr, Albury Salivating media A republic, Pete (“Harry and Meghan return to splendour”, August 30)? That’s as pointless as royalty. The quaint notion that we need a head of state has no governance imperatives of any great merit. Just scrap the old-fashioned concept. Though, on second thoughts, everyone loves showbusiness, so why not keep the monarchy going for its entertainment value. (And remember, it’s far cheaper if we time-share the Pommy version.) Brian Haisman, Winmalee

Emergency services were called to Gardiner Park in Banksia, about 12 kilometres south of Sydney’s CBD, about 1.20pm on Saturday after the jumping castle became airborne, a NSW Ambulance spokeswoman said. The children were taken to Sydney Children’s Hospital after being treated by paramedics at the scene. A preschool-aged boy and girl suffered head injuries, while a baby was treated for minor injuries. A woman was also taken to hospital with minor injuries, the spokeswoman said. All three children were in a stable condition. Be the first to know when major news happens.

World.title: ‘Survivable pockets’: Australian tunnel expert arrives in Nepal, hopeful of more rescues
World.content:
WorldAsiaFloods ‘Survivable pockets’: Australian tunnel expert arrives in Nepal, hopeful of more rescues Michael McGowan Updated September 5, 2026 — 9:55pm ,first published 4:50pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Kathmandu: An Australian tunnelling expert who helped to orchestrate the extraordinary rescue of two workers from a hydropower tunnel in northern Nepal is headed for the disaster zone, firmly believing there is still hope of finding more survivors trapped hundreds of metres below the earth. After helping to lead the rescue operation remotely from his home in Victoria this week, engineer and geologist Arnold Dix flew into Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu, late on Friday night (Nepal time). Australian tunnelling expert Arnold Dix has arrived in disaster-stricken Nepal believing there is still hope of finding survivors. Justin McManus It comes as rescuers in Nepal pulled a Chinese national alive from a hydropower tunnel on Saturday, according to a social media post by the country’s prime minister’s office, and in a separate effort, rescuers pulled a woman out alive from a house 10 days after floods hit Nuwakot town, a Nepalese army spokesperson said. The latest tunnel rescue brings the total to three workers pulled alive from the Trishuli hydropower project. Two Nepalese workers were rescued from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower plant on Friday.



Nepal’s army said a joint team of Nepalese military personnel and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre tunnel, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. In flood-hit Nuwakot town, a woman was rescued alive from a house, Nepal’s army spokesperson said Saturday. Officials said she was airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment. Loading Images released by Nepal’s army showed rescuers finding the woman covered in mud inside the damaged house. They gave her bottled water before pulling her to safety, wrapped in a gray blanket. While the odds are against Dix and the rest of the global team of experts providing advice to Nepalese authorities on the ongoing rescue mission, he said that he absolutely believed there was hope of finding more survivors under the earth some 10 days after the devastating floods.



“In the game of paper, scissor, rock, human, the odds aren’t good. But yeah [there are] survivable pockets, absolutely, and that’s what we’re aiming for,” he said. On Saturday morning, he boarded a helicopter for the Chilime Hydropower Plant, high in the Himalayan valley and close to the Chinese border. There he will meet with members of the Indian rescue team he worked with after 41 men were trapped in the Silkyara Bend-Barkot tunnel in the Himalayas in 2023. Dix has also worked on other rescue missions, including at Ground Zero after September 11. “We’re just like the underground rescue buddies,” he told this masthead just ahead of his flight on Saturday. A helicopter drops search and rescue teams at the exit tunnel of the Chilime Hydropower Plant during the week. Kate Geraghty



It has been more than a week since devastating floods tore through Nepal, causing tsunami-like waves of water, rock and debris that has resulted in 1294 confirmed deaths. More than 5000 people are still missing, including 583 foreign nationals. The Chinese government has reported 31 confirmed deaths and 531 missing – including 261 foreign nationals – on the Tibet side of the border. Related Article Floods At first, the smell is overwhelming. Then, they open the book of the dead Among those still unaccounted for are workers believed to be trapped inside the hydropower tunnels that Nepal has used to harness the fast-flowing waters of the Himalayas and increase the blackout-prone country’s power generation. Nepal’s Independent Power Producers’ Association said during the week that it believed ​at least eight people could be trapped in the Chilime tunnel. It is one of seven hydropower tunnels at which rescue operations are taking place, with hundreds of workers believed to have been trapped. Until Friday, Dix had helped the effort remotely from Australia, unable to board a plane during the crucial hours and days after the disaster.



“Time was of the essence,” he said. “I couldn’t lose two days because I knew they had to start digging.” They had focused on the Trishuli 3A ­hydropower project, and he said the rescue of mechanical foreman Sanjay Sah and mechanical supervisor Kabir Maharjan from the tunnel on Friday was confirmation of the work he and others had been doing throughout the week. “[It means] we’ve got survivable zones in there,” Dix said. “That confirms our theory, if you like. Until that, it was a theory. We really didn’t know if it was survivable in there.” It makes him believe there could “absolutely” be more workers still alive inside. “Of course, the odds are against us. Like, you wouldn’t, you know, go to the casino and play the house on these things normally,” he said.



Dix and his team had relied on engineering drawings of the massive hydropower structures that Nepal uses to generate electricity, as well as satellite imagery, to identify the survivable pockets inside. “The world has never had something like this,” he said. Arnold Dix has previously helped to orchestrate the rescue of 41 Indian workers who were trapped for 17 days after a landslide in the Himalayas. “We’re not dealing with tunnels that might’ve collapsed. They won’t have. We’re dealing with tunnels that are filled up with stuff. “It’s this explosive inrush. It just turns the textbook on its head … that’s why the rescue yesterday was so important because we’ve never dealt with anything like this.”



While they were confident in their theory, the challenge of digging into the deep, unstable earth, where “rocks the size of cars” had barrelled into the tunnels, presented many challenges of its own. Related Article Floods In Nepal, hope gives way to grief. Few are counting on miracles “That’s on the one hand, and the other hand, [the question was] how the hell are we going to get in there to get them?” he said. “You have to find a reason to use your resources, which is where might people be alive? That’s the first question, and then your second question is, ‘OK, now, how do we get them?’ “You can’t just dig everywhere. You’ve seen the destruction here, so you’ve got to be very specific in what you do.”

World.title: Two sin bins and a last-minute match-winner: Cronulla’s season continues to slip
World.content:
SportNRLNRL 2026 Two sin bins and a last-minute match-winner: Cronulla’s season continues to slip Billie Eder September 5, 2026 — 9:47pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

So long as Cronulla escaped Saturday night without any injuries or suspensions, they could have considered it a win, regardless of the score. But that’s not what happened. Instead, the Sharks went into the 79th minute of the match ahead on the scoreboard, despite having two men sent to the bin in the opening 10 minutes, before a Harry Grant flick pass to Trent Loiero clawed back victory for Melbourne on the siren, 24-20. Loading To say it was a deflating end for the Cronulla faithful inside Shark Park would be an understatement.



Now, the Sharks head into their elimination final against the Cowboys next Saturday on a two-game losing streak, after an embarrassing loss to Parramatta which squandered their chance of a top-four finish and resulted in coach Craig Fitzgibbon taking his frustrations out on a computer monitor. Fitzgibbon was unhappy again after the match. But not for losing the game – for the officiating of referee Todd Smith who called 18 infringements in the first half alone, and for both of Melbourne’s opening tries. Hugo Peel’s opener came from a forward pass and the second from Sua Fa’alogo appeared to be grounded on the dead-ball line. Sua Faalogo scores Melbourne’s second try of the night. Getty Images “You’ve been around as long as I have. If you don’t know what a forward pass looks like at this point of your career, I don’t know either,” Fitzgibbon said to reporters. The positive for Cronulla is they get their star players back next week, with Nicho Hynes, Braydon Trindall, Blayke Brailey and KL Iro all having been rested against Melbourne.



It’s fair to say Cronulla will need far more convincing and consistent performances if they hope to contend for the premiership a decade after the club lifted the trophy for the first and only time. The Sharks will start as favourites for their clash against the Cowboys, but it will be Trindall’s first game back after three weeks off following a shoulder injury, and the match will likely be held at the more neutral venue of Allianz Stadium rather than their beloved ‘Shark Park’. Saturday was anything but reassuring for Cronulla fans after Melbourne stormed to a 12-0 lead following the double sin-binning. Debutant Michael Gabrael was sent to the bin in the fifth minute of the match – and the first tackle of his NRL career – for a shoulder charge on Siulagi Tuimalatu-Brown.



Siulagi Tuimalatu-Brown was eventually stretchered off and taken to hospital. Getty Images The Melbourne winger was stretchered off and taken to hospital for a precautionary check after experiencing neck pain. Then Ronaldo Mulitalo left Cronulla with only 11 men on the field after he was also sent to the bin for striking Melbourne hooker Harry Grant in a melee. Despite the brain snap, Multialo should also be available for selection next week. However, Cronulla will have to wait for the match review committee’s verdict on a possible hip-drop tackle by Addin Fonua-Blake on Cooper Clarke.



Cronulla celebrate Billy Burns try. Getty Images The Sharks fought to get back into the contest and went into the sheds ahead 18-12 at half-time after tries to Sione Katoa, Riley Jones and Billy Burns. Related Article NRL 2026 Warriors pip Manly to give Penrith minor premiership edge; new No.7 shines for Raiders Cronulla’s comeback coincided with Melbourne halfback Jarhome Hughes succumbing to a hamstring injury – a concern for the Kiwis with World Cup selection around the corner. The Sharks appeared to have the match sealed up with a penalty goal from Niwhai Puru the difference between the sides heading into the final minute of the game.



But Melbourne’s never-say-die trio of Cameron Munster, Grant and Sua Fa’alogo managed to find a spark in the final minute of the match to set up Loiero’s try and save Craig Bellamy the embarrassment of his worst win-loss ratio since the 2002 season. World.title: Swans fear worst after ‘devastating’ Mills injury mars epic victory over Lions
World.content:
Loading

The pride and jubilation that followed Sydney’s extraordinary upset victory over the Brisbane Lions has been tempered by what is expected to be confirmed as a serious knee injury to Swans skipper Callum Mills. Sydney coach Dean Cox said Mills, who was helped off the field midway through the first quarter of the qualifying final, had suffered a bad knee injury and while he did not specify that it was a torn anterior cruciate ligament, this was virtually confirmed by the coach. Loading Typically, the scans that follow ACL injuries confirm the suspicions of club medicos. If he has ruptured the ACL, Mills will miss most, and potentially all, of the 2027 season. “Obviously, not expecting great news on Callum,” said Cox, who was proud of his team’s stirring victory in the face of suspensions to five key players.



“And we’ll in the next couple of days find out the extent of that, which is devastating for him and the footy club. We’ll do whatever we can to support him through whatever it is that he will go through. “There’s that and for the maturity of the group, to see what happened – it didn’t look great from the outset – and to rally and stay on task and focus on what they had to do was a credit to them.” Callum Mills was on crutches after injuring his knee in the Swans’ win. AFL Photos Asked to confirm that it was an ACL rupture, Cox said: “It’s a knee, yeah. So we’re not sure exactly the full extent of it. It doesn’t look good, and we’ll work out exactly what it is in the next day or two.” Cox said the players had been galvanised to perform in this final, in which the Swans kicked an explosive six goals to one opening burst and built momentum throughout the game, as Logan McDonald, Charlie Curnow and Tom Papley booted a staggering 16 goals between them.



McDonald said Sydney’s players did not speak about Mills’ injury after he went off. Such is his importance to the side that they did not have to mention it – the mere sight of Mills on the big screen giving Swans fans a thumbs-up from the bench was enough. “We’ll get around him this week,” McDonald said. “He’s always so selfless. Nothing’s about him. He’s just put the club first straight away. We’ll put our arms around him because he means so much to us as a player.” Loading The fact they got the job done with Mills off the field for more than three quarters was proof, Papley said, that Sydney’s tactical plan under Cox did not rely on individuals – whether that was their skipper or the sidelined “Pullman Five”. “I always believed. Not once did I think we couldn’t win,” he said. “We always believed inside the four walls. It didn’t matter who was out because our system doesn’t require talent. It’s hard work.



“Our system, sometimes it might look flashy, and it’s a lot of talent, but the backbone of it – 80 per cent of it, 90 percent of it – is hard work and desire and pressure and doing your bit for the team. “We won today without Millsy, so that adds to the win as well. It is what it is. We’ll regroup, we’ve got a couple of weeks to work out who comes in for Millsy, but we’ll get to work.” Charlie Curnow and coach Dean Cox after a win for the ages. AFL Photos Added Cox: “The story’s not finished yet for our season.” Meanwhile, Brisbane Lions coach Chris Fagan took aim at his players for not heeding his warnings about underestimating the undermanned Swans.



“I’m not sure my players believe me,” Fagan said. “To be honest with you, I tried very hard this week to convince our players it was going to be a tough game. We’re going to the SCG, it’s Sydney’s home ground. But somewhere back in the deep recesses of their mind, I just wonder whether they really thought it was going to be as hard as what it was. “Did you really think that Sydney were going to be that good, or did you think it was going to be maybe a walk in the park? Because that’s how it had been painted by all and sundry that’s following football. And probably quite rightly so. Callum Mills of the Swans celebrates victory with teammates. via Getty Images “But you can never underestimate the human spirit and that’s what Sydney displayed plenty of tonight. They showed human spirit, backs against the walls, playing against a team that’s been in pretty good form and gave us a football lesson. They won because they were tougher, harder, they ran harder, they used the ball well. They were excellent and they should be really proud of their effort and I’m sure they will be. We’re not. We’ve got work to do.” Crisis-torn Swans produce one of the great AFL finals upsets over Lions



Vince Rugari Many questions have been asked in relation to the Sydney Swans since that fateful Monday morning at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne three weeks ago. Here’s one nobody bothered to ask: what happens if they actually win? The Swans’s win over Brisbane was one of the greatest finals victories in the club’s history. Getty Images Nobody bothered to ask because, before Saturday, the idea was preposterous. Outside of the Swans themselves, nobody genuinely thought they could win this game. Not a qualifying final against two-time reigning premiers Brisbane, who have lost only one game since May. Not without five of their best players. Not after everything that’s happened in the last month.



As soon as the Swans suspended the ‘Pullman Five’, a line was drawn through the club’s name by virtually the entire AFL industry. Their odds blew out with bookmakers and they sunk to the bottom of everyone’s finals power rankings. Their own chairman, Andrew Pridham, seemed to think they were as good as done: their season had been “torpedoed”, in his words, when those season-ending bans were meted out to Isaac Heeney, Nick Blakey, Chad Warner, Riley Bice and James Jordon for breaching club standards. Even their own fans seemed to agree, with only 37,261 turning up at the SCG on Saturday afternoon. It was the Swans’ lowest finals crowd at home in more than a decade. Logan McDonald kicked a career-high six goals. AFL Photos via Getty Images Perhaps the Lions believed it, too. Because only that could explain the way they turned up, as if they expected the Swans to simply roll over and accept their assigned fate. They did not.



And now, after Sydney’s stirring 53-point victory, one of the great AFL finals upsets, we are in uncharted territory: this crisis-torn football club is somehow just one win away from a grand final appearance, having absorbed every bit of angst and scrutiny directed their way and channelled it to their advantage. “I’d be writing them off at your peril,” Alastair Clarkson said here two weeks ago in what proved to be one of his final utterances as North Melbourne coach. Prophetic words. Tom Papley had one of the best games of his career. AFL Photos The Lions simply could not handle Sydney’s hunger, intent and efficiency, which overwhelmed Brisbane’s most celebrated names and punched massive holes in their much-vaunted defence. The Swans kicked six of the first seven goals of the match to leave the visitors stunned; that margin remained intact for practically the whole afternoon and proved to be the difference. They prevailed 21.15 (141) to 13.10 (88). Every time Brisbane tried to reel them in, the swarming Swans had a response of some kind that kept alive the belief that was sustaining them. They simply wanted it more, whereas the Lions, having tasted the ultimate success twice before, resembled a champion boxer who got old overnight. Lachie Neale, the pre-eminent example, had just 18 disposals and two clearances, none of them important. Brisbane have overcome bad finals defeats before, but this one was a doozy.



Tom Papley started the day under an injury cloud after appearing to tweak his calf in the warm-up. He finished it with five goals, each of them somehow worth more than six points because of the energy he generated with his celebrations. Two came in a blitz at the end of the third quarter which pushed Sydney’s lead to a scarcely believable 46 points at three-quarter time, capped by Errol Gulden’s sensational individual effort from the centre bounce. Logan McDonald produced the game of his career, bagging six goals. His first was the first of the match, and came at the end of a chain which featured a one-handed grab in the middle by Charlie Curnow over Darcy Gardiner. The last came from a set shot on the boundary in the dying moments. (Curnow also booted five.) The Brisbane Lions simply could not handle Sydney’s hunger, intent and efficiency. via Getty Images Almost everything went right for the Swans. Almost. Something went very wrong midway through the opening term, when captain Callum Mills twisted his knee in ominous fashion as he tried to corral Will Ashcroft on the boundary line. Confirmation that he would take no further part in the game suitably arrived, via the club’s X account, with a crying emoji at the end of the sentence as punctuation. Coach Dean Cox spoke about what losing the skipper to the team after the game.



“To lose your captain early, to rally, execute the roles they wanted to play at. I couldn’t be prouder,” Cox told Kayo Sports. Related Article Live

AFL 2026 AFL LIVE: Crows fans stand for their coach as the Bulldogs’ season ends in an elimination final “We’ve worked hard on this game style for 10 months and we want to make sure that anyone that comes into the team can execute their role and do what is required, when it is required and they did that in spades.” That Sydney still won without him, and after seeing his shattered visage on the big screen, further underlined the value of this performance. But a crueller twist of fate was hard to imagine. Mills had risen to the moment as the Pullman scandal had demanded, leading admirably with both his words in press conferences and his actions on the field. He also missed Sydney’s last grand final appearance through injury in 2024; this was his first consistent season of football in three years. In the absence of the five banned players, for all sorts of reasons, Mills was one of Sydney’s most important players. Whatever they do next, they will almost certainly have to do in his absence. But you’d be crazy to put a limit on what that could be.

World.title: Qantas flight diverted to Christchurch after 'engine issue'
World.content:
A Qantas flight from Queenstown had to be diverted to Christchurch on Saturday afternoon, after it experienced an "engine issue" after takeoff.

The Boeing 737-800 aircraft had just become airborne when the incident occurred.

Witnesses reported hearing banging noises. Video footage on social media appeared to show flames coming from an engine.

Nic Chamberlain was among those in Queenstown who saw flames and heard a series of loud noises.

"It was like just shoots of orange flames shooting out the back.

"You can tell it was coming out of the left engine," he told RNZ.

There was a delay before the loud noises followed, he said.

"This was kind of like rapid succession boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom. And then it was loud enough that everyone kind of turned their heads and looked to see what the noise was," he said.

Flight QF122 touched down safely at Christchurch Airport at about 5pm on Saturday. There were no reports of injuries.

RNZ understands about 160 passengers were on board.

A Qantas spokesperson said the incident was under investigation.

"One of our flights to Sydney experienced a suspected engine issue after take-off from Queenstown this afternoon and the aircraft diverted to Christchurch.

"Our pilots are highly trained to manage situations like this and the aircraft landed safely.

"We know this would have been a distressing experience for passengers and will be contacting all customers to provide support," they said.

Earlier, the Civil Aviation Authority said bird strike caused the incident. It has since amended that statement, saying that it was unable to confirm the cause at this stage.

Hato Hone St John said it was notified of a flight diversion at 4.25pm and multiple ambulance resources responded to Christchurch Airport as a standard procedure.

A spokesperson said St John had not been required to assess or treat anyone, and all ambulance units had since been stood down.

Fire and Emergency New Zealand records show an aircraft emergency was reported at Invercargill Airport at 4.12pm, with Invercargill and Kingswell crews attending.

It is understood the flight was initially expected to divert to Invercargill before continuing to Christchurch.

World.title: Fullback Taine Tuaupiki saves Warriors with hattrick of tries over Sea Eagles
World.content:
Fullback Taine Tuaupiki - who wasn't originally named to play - has saved NZ Warriors' bacon with a hattrick of tries in a desperate 31-30 win over Manly Sea Eagles to keep their NRL minor premiership hopes alive.

The home side needed a late field goal from Chanel Harris-Tavita to snatch victory from their dogged opponents and now await the result between Penrith Panthers and Wests Tigers on Sunday, which will determine the winners of the regular-season crown.

Off to a slow start, the Warriors trailled 12-4 after 20 minutes, but rattled on the next four tries - two to Tuaupiki - to lead 24-12 just after halftime.

Tuaupiki was initially named on the interchange bench as backline cover, but entered the starting line-up when centre Leka Halasima withdrew with an ankle injury 24 hours out.

His inclusion saw Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad shifted to the wing, where he also had a try double in that 20-point run before the Sea Eagles came charging back.

As the match continued, star fullback Tom Trbojevic started to stamp his class on the game, creating chances for those around him.

Manly scored the next three tries and almost had a fourth, which was disallowed for a penalty back on halfway, to grab a 30-24 advantage late in the second half.

Tuaupiki brought the Warriors back on level terms, slicing against the grain to score next to the posts and then converting from in front.

The Warriors had two tries ruled out in the closing minutes, with Harris-Tavita and prop Tanner Stowers-Smith both crossing, and Harris-Tavita also had a field goal attempt charged down.

With the final seconds ticking down, halfback Te Maire Martin received the ball in front of the posts, but was run off his kick. On the next play, Harris-Tavita had more room to operate and duly slotted in the gamewinner.

Victory sees the Warriors set a club record of 18-6 for the season and puts them two points clear at the top of the NRL table.

Penrith can still secure the minor premiership with a three-point win over the 15th-placed Tigers.
